definition_zh: n. 注释；批注；（数据或基因的）标注
definition_en: A note added to a text, image or dataset to explain or comment on it; in biology, the labelling of features in a genome sequence.
core_image: 在正文旁边空白处写下的一行小字
scene: 他在页边写满了自己的疑问和补充。 Every annotation in the margin is in his own hand.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：页边空白处那些解释与评论的小字就是 annotation，是加在原文之外的注记。

pos.zh: 注释；批注；标注

senses.title: A note added to a text
senses.definition: an explanatory or critical note written beside or below a passage
senses.definitionCN: 写在一段文字旁边或下方的解释性或评论性注记
senses.example: The edition carries annotations on every page.
senses.exampleCN: 这个版本每一页都有注释。
senses.why: Latin annotare meant to mark beside, from ad-, to, and nota, a mark; the note is literally placed next to the text rather than inside it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 annotare 意为「在旁边做标记」，由 ad-「向」与 nota「标记」构成；注记字面上是放在文本旁边，而不是文本里面。

senses.title: Labelling in data and genomes
senses.titleCN: 数据与基因组中的标注
senses.definition: the tagging of features in a dataset or sequence so that a machine or reader can use them
senses.definitionCN: 为数据集或序列中的特征打标签，使机器或读者能够使用
senses.example: Genome annotation identifies where each gene begins.
senses.exampleCN: 基因组注释标出每个基因的起始位置。
senses.why: The same act of marking beside is now done at scale: the sequence is the text, and the labels are the marginal notes.
senses.whyCN: 同一种「在旁边标记」的动作如今大规模进行：序列就是正文，标签就是页边注。

intro.en: Annotation is Latin annotatio, from annotare, to mark beside, from ad-, to, and nota, a mark. The word keeps the picture of a note written in the margin.
intro.cn: annotation 来自拉丁语 annotatio，出自 annotare「在旁边做标记」，由 ad-「向」与 nota「标记」构成。这个词保留了「在页边写注」的画面。

items.en: Latin ad- meant to or toward, and assimilates to an- before n, which is why the word has a double n.
items.cn: 拉丁语 ad- 意为「向、朝」，在 n 前同化为 an-，这就是该词有双写 n 的原因。

items.en: Latin nota meant a mark, sign or letter, and gives note, notation, notable and denote.
items.cn: 拉丁语 nota 意为「标记、符号、字母」，产生 note、notation、notable 与 denote。

items.en: Annotare meant to mark beside or add a note to, the working verb of scholars reading with a pen in hand.
items.cn: annotare 意为「在旁边标记、加注」，是学者手执笔阅读时的常用动词。

items.en: Annotatio was the noun of action, and English took annotation in the sixteenth century for the note itself as well as the act.
items.cn: annotatio 是动作名词，英语在 16 世纪借入 annotation，既指注记本身，也指加注这一行为。

items.en: Modern English extends annotation to code, images and genome sequences, and the verb annotate is now common in data work.
items.cn: 现代英语把 annotation 扩展到代码、图像与基因组序列，动词 annotate 在数据工作中已很常见。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the nota family and contrasts denotation; the near-meaning group lists other words for an added note.
note.cn: 形近组保留 nota 词族并与 denotation 对照；近义组列出其他表示附加注记的词。

entries.definition: To add notes to a text.
A person who adds notes.
Provided with notes.
The literal meaning of a word.
A short written comment.
A brief explanation of a difficult word.
A sustained set of explanations.
A note printed at the bottom of a page.

normalIntro.en: Annotation is ad- plus nota plus -tion: a mark placed beside the text.
normalIntro.cn: annotation 就是 ad- 加 nota 加 -tion：放在文本旁边的一个标记。

normal.en: The verb is annotate, the person an annotator.
normal.cn: 动词是 annotate，人是 annotator。

normal.en: It is countable: an annotation, several annotations.
normal.cn: 它可数：an annotation、several annotations。

normal.en: An annotated edition is one with notes added.
normal.cn: annotated edition 指加了注释的版本。

normal.en: Do not confuse annotation with denotation, literal meaning.
normal.cn: 别把 annotation 与 denotation「字面意义」混淆。

normal.en: Genome annotation is the standard term in biology.
normal.cn: genome annotation 是生物学中的标准术语。

abstract.en: Picture a margin crowded with small handwriting.
abstract.cn: 想象页边挤满了细小的手写字。

abstract.en: Imagine a sequence with coloured labels above each gene.
abstract.cn: 想象一段序列，每个基因上方都有彩色标签。

abstract.en: Think of a reader talking back to the page.
abstract.cn: 想象一个读者对着书页回话。

examples.en: Each annotation explains a difficult allusion.
examples.cn: 每条注释解释一处难懂的典故。

examples.en: The team spent a year on genome annotation.
examples.cn: 团队花了一年做基因组注释。

examples.en: He annotated the manuscript in red ink.
examples.cn: 他用红墨水给手稿加注。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：an「向」+ not「标记」+ ation「动作」——朝着正文旁边做标记，就是注释、批注。

root: 拉丁语 ad-「向」在 n 前同化为 an-，加 nota「标记」构成 annotare「在旁边标记」，动作名词 annotatio 入英语为 annotation，字面即「加在旁边的注记」。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are one mark placed beside: a scholar note in a margin, and a label attached to data or a sequence.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项是同一个放在旁边的标记：学者写在页边的注，以及贴在数据或序列上的标签。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line of small writing in the margin beside the text
core.cn: 核心意象：正文旁边空白处的一行小字

branches.en: A page of notes in a student hand.
branches.cn: 一页学生笔迹的注记。

branches.en: A footnote explaining an allusion.
branches.cn: 一条解释典故的脚注。

branches.en: Labels marking each gene start.
branches.cn: 标出每个基因起点的标签。

branches.en: Boxes drawn around objects in images.
branches.cn: 在图像中物体周围画的框。

branches.en: Both add a mark beside the original.
branches.cn: 两者都在原件旁边加标记。

intro.en: Annotation is ad- plus nota plus -ation, and the nota root builds note, notation, denote and notable.
intro.cn: annotation 是 ad- 加 nota 加 -ation，nota 词根还构成 note、notation、denote 与 notable。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is nota, a mark, and annotare, to mark beside; ad- becomes an- before n, giving the double n.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语层次是 nota「标记」与 annotare「在旁边标记」；ad- 在 n 前变成 an-，形成双写 n。

latinEntries.exampleCN: nota 产生 note 与 notation。

latinEntries.example: Annotatio is the noun of action.

definition_zh: n. 圆形露天剧场；（美）阶梯式讲堂；环形阶梯座位区
definition_en: An open circular building with tiers of seats rising around a central space; also a lecture hall or a valley shaped like one.
core_image: 一圈圈石阶围着中央那块空地
scene: 学生们坐在山坡的阶梯座位上听露天讲座。 The lecture was held in a natural amphitheatre.
sceneCN: 第 2 个义项：这里不是古罗马建筑，而是形状像圆形剧场的天然山坡阶梯座位区，讲座就在那里举行。

pos.zh: 圆形露天剧场；阶梯式讲堂

senses.title: The ancient circular building
senses.definition: an open oval or circular structure with rising tiers of seats around a central arena
senses.definitionCN: 露天的椭圆形或圆形建筑，中央竞技场四周环绕着逐层升高的座位
senses.example: The amphitheatre could hold twenty thousand spectators.
senses.exampleCN: 这座圆形剧场能容纳两万名观众。
senses.why: Greek amphi- means on both sides and theatron means a place for seeing, so the word names a place where you can see from every side.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 amphi- 意为「在两边」，theatron 意为「观看之所」，所以这个词命名的是一个从每一侧都能观看的地方。

senses.title: Any tiered ring of seats
senses.definition: a lecture hall, hillside or valley whose seats or slopes rise in a semicircle
senses.definitionCN: 座位或坡面呈半圆形逐层升高的讲堂、山坡或谷地
senses.example: The village sits in a natural amphitheatre of hills.
senses.exampleCN: 这个村庄坐落在群山环抱的天然环形谷地中。
senses.why: The shape, not the stone, carries the meaning: once the tiers curve around a centre, the name transfers to lecture halls and landscapes.
senses.whyCN: 承载含义的是形状而非石材：只要阶梯围绕一个中心弯曲，这个名称就转移到讲堂与地形上。

intro.en: Amphitheatre is Greek amphitheatron, from amphi-, on both sides, and theatron, a place for seeing. Latin took it as amphitheatrum, and English kept both the -tre and -ter spellings.
intro.cn: amphitheatre 来自希腊语 amphitheatron，由 amphi-「在两边」与 theatron「观看之所」构成。拉丁语借为 amphitheatrum，英语保留了 -tre 与 -ter 两种拼写。

items.en: Amphi meant on both sides or around, and appears in amphibious and amphora as well as this word.
items.cn: amphi 意为「在两边、环绕」，除本词外也出现在 amphibious 与 amphora 中。

items.en: Theatron meant a place for seeing, from theaomai, to look at. A theatre was originally the seating, not the stage.
items.cn: theatron 意为「观看之所」，来自 theaomai「观看」。剧院最初指的是座位区，而不是舞台。

items.en: Greek amphitheatron joined the two pieces for a structure where spectators surround the action instead of facing it from one side.
items.cn: 希腊语 amphitheatron 把两个部件拼合，指观众环绕而非单侧面对表演场地的建筑。

items.en: Latin amphitheatrum named the Roman buildings, and the ruins kept the word alive across Europe long after the games stopped.
items.cn: 拉丁语 amphitheatrum 指那些罗马建筑，竞技停止很久之后，遗址仍让这个词在欧洲各地流传。

items.en: English took the word in the fourteenth century, keeps -tre in Britain and -ter in America, and extends it to any tiered semicircle.
items.cn: 英语在 14 世纪借入该词，英国用 -tre、美国用 -ter，并把它扩展到任何阶梯半圆形空间。

note.en: The look-alike group handles the two spellings and the near opening amphora; the near-meaning group lists other venues built around a centre.
note.cn: 形近组处理两种拼写与开头相近的 amphora；近义组列出其他围绕中心而建的场所。

entries.definition: The same word in American spelling.
Arranged in rising curved tiers.
entries.definitionCN: 呈逐层升高弧形排列的。

entries.definition: A building for plays, seats facing one way.
entries.definitionCN: 演剧的建筑，座位朝一个方向。

entries.definition: A two-handled ancient jar.
The open space where events take place.
A large sports ground with tiered seats.
entries.definitionCN: 带阶梯座位的大型运动场。

entries.definition: The part of a hall where the audience sits.
A very large ancient amphitheatre.

normalIntro.en: Amphitheatre is amphi plus theatre: a theatre you can watch from every side.
normalIntro.cn: amphitheatre 就是 amphi 加 theatre：一个从每一侧都能观看的剧院。

normal.en: A theatre faces one way; an amphitheatre wraps around.
normal.cn: theatre 朝一个方向，amphitheatre 环绕一圈。

normal.en: British spelling ends -tre, American ends -ter.
normal.cn: 英式拼写以 -tre 结尾，美式以 -ter 结尾。

normal.en: The plural is amphitheatres, with a plain s.
normal.cn: 复数是 amphitheatres，直接加 s。

normal.en: A natural amphitheatre is a bowl of hills, not a building.
normal.cn: natural amphitheatre 指碗状群山，不是建筑。

normal.en: Do not confuse amphitheatre with amphora, a jar.
normal.cn: 别把 amphitheatre 与 amphora「陶罐」混淆。

abstract.en: Picture stone rings rising around a patch of sand.
abstract.cn: 想象一圈圈石阶围绕一片沙地升起。

abstract.en: Imagine a hillside where every student can see the speaker.
abstract.cn: 想象一片山坡，每个学生都能看见讲者。

abstract.en: Think of a village held in the palm of a valley.
abstract.cn: 想象一个村庄被托在谷地的手心里。

examples.en: The amphitheatre survives almost intact after two thousand years.
examples.cn: 这座圆形剧场历经两千年几乎完好无损。

examples.en: Concerts are staged in the amphitheatre each summer.
examples.cn: 每年夏天都在露天剧场举办音乐会。

examples.en: The medical school built a small amphitheatre for demonstrations.
examples.cn: 医学院建了一间小型阶梯讲堂用于演示。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：amphi「两边、环绕」+ theatre「剧院」——座位绕着中央转一圈的剧院，就是圆形剧场。

root: 希腊语 amphi「环绕」+ theatron「观看之所」构成 amphitheatron，拉丁语借为 amphitheatrum，英语作 amphitheatre（美 amphitheater），字面即「四面都能观看的场所」。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are one shape: the Roman stone ring, and any hillside or hall that copies its curved tiers.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项是同一个形状：罗马的石环，以及任何模仿其弧形阶梯的山坡或厅堂。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: stone rings rising around one open centre
core.cn: 核心意象：一圈圈石阶围着一块开阔中心升起

branches.en: A Roman ruin with sand in the middle.
branches.cn: 中央铺沙的罗马遗址。

branches.en: Twenty thousand seats facing inward.
branches.cn: 两万个朝内的座位。

branches.en: A lecture hall with curved rows.
branches.cn: 座位呈弧形排列的讲堂。

branches.en: A valley that holds a village like a bowl.
branches.cn: 像碗一样托住村庄的谷地。

branches.en: The same curve, in stone then in land.
branches.cn: 同一条弧线，先在石头上，再在地形上。

intro.en: Amphitheatre keeps amphi- and the seeing root thea-, and the same pieces build theatre, audience and auditorium.
intro.cn: amphitheatre 保留 amphi- 与「观看」词根 thea-，同样的部件还构成 theatre、audience 与 auditorium。

latinIntro.en: Greek amphitheatron became Latin amphitheatrum; the -um ending was dropped in French and English, leaving -tre or -ter.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 amphitheatron 变成拉丁语 amphitheatrum；-um 词尾在法语与英语中脱落，留下 -tre 或 -ter。

latinEntries.meaning: a place seen from all sides

definition_zh: adj. 令人敬畏的；引起惊叹的；（口语）极好的；了不起的
definition_en: Inspiring awe, wonder or fear; in informal use, extremely good or impressive.
core_image: 站在崖边一时说不出话的那种震动
scene: 峡谷边缘风很大，孩子们一时都说不出话。 The view from the canyon rim was awesome, and the children fell silent.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：awesome 指景象或力量宏大得令人敬畏，带有震动与肃然之意。

pos.zh: 令人敬畏的；极好的

collocations.zh: 重大得令人敬畏的责任

forms.label: 形容词原级（比较级用 more）

senses.title: Inspiring awe
senses.definition: so large, powerful or grand that it fills a person with wonder mixed with fear
senses.definitionCN: 宏大、有力或壮丽到让人既惊叹又心生畏惧
senses.example: The storm showed the awesome force of the sea.
senses.exampleCN: 那场风暴显示了海洋令人敬畏的力量。
senses.why: Awesome is awe plus -some, so it describes whatever produces awe, a feeling older than admiration.
senses.whyCN: awesome 是 awe 加 -some，因此它描述任何能引出敬畏之物，而敬畏这种感受比欣赏更古老。

senses.title: Extremely good
senses.definition: in informal speech, very good or impressive, with the fear drained out of the original sense
senses.definitionCN: 在口语中指非常好或很出色，原义中的畏惧已被抽掉
senses.example: That was an awesome concert.
senses.exampleCN: 那场音乐会太棒了。
senses.why: Young speakers kept the intensity but dropped the dread, so a word for terror became a word of praise.
senses.whyCN: 年轻使用者保留了强度却舍去了畏惧，于是一个表恐惧的词变成了赞美词。

intro.en: Awesome is awe plus -some; awe comes from Old Norse agi, terror, which replaced an older English word for fear of the divine.
intro.cn: awesome 是 awe 加 -some；awe 来自古诺斯语 agi「恐惧」，它取代了更早的英语中表示对神明畏惧的词。

items.en: A root meaning to be anxious or choked lies behind words of dread and narrowness.
items.cn: 一个表示「焦虑、窒息」的词根支撑着恐惧与狭窄类的词。

items.en: Old Norse agi meant terror or discipline, the fear that keeps a person in order.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 agi 意为「恐惧、约束」，即使人守规矩的那种怕。

items.en: Northern Middle English took the word as aghe, dread of God or of a lord.
items.cn: 北部中古英语借作 aghe，指对神或领主的畏惧。

items.en: The form settled as awe, and the phrase stand in awe kept the older fear.
items.cn: 形式定为 awe，而表示肃然敬畏的短语保留了更早的畏惧义。

items.en: English added -some in the 1590s to describe what inspires that dread.
items.cn: 英语在 1590 年代加上 -some，用来描述引出这种畏惧之物。

items.en: American youth speech from the 1960s turned awesome into general praise.
items.cn: 1960 年代起的美国青年口语把 awesome 变成泛用的赞美词。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the awe family, including the cousin that went bad; the near-meaning group lists words for grand and for excellent.
note.cn: 形近组保留 awe 词族，包括那个走坏方向的近亲；近义组列出表示宏大与表示极好的词。

entries.definition: Wonder mixed with fear.
Very bad or unpleasant.
Stopped by sudden wonder.
entries.definitionCN: 被 sudden 惊叹震住的。

entries.definition: Off course, not as planned.
Splendidly large or fine.
So striking it stops the breath.
Causing respect through size.
Of the highest quality.

normalIntro.en: Awesome is awe plus -some: full of awe, whether that awe is dread at a cliff or delight at a concert.
normalIntro.cn: awesome 是 awe 加 -some：充满敬畏，无论是在崖边的震慑还是在音乐会的兴奋。

normal.en: Awe once meant fear, not admiration.
normal.cn: awe 早先指畏惧，不是欣赏。

normal.en: Awful took the bad road, awesome the good.
normal.cn: awful 走了坏的方向，awesome 走了好的方向。

normal.en: Formal writing keeps the grand sense.
normal.cn: 正式书面语保留宏大之义。

normal.en: Speech uses it as general praise.
normal.cn: 口语把它当作泛用赞美。

normal.en: The noun phrase is stand in awe of.
normal.cn: 名词短语是 stand in awe of。

abstract.en: Picture a rim where words fail you.
abstract.cn: 想象一处让你说不出话的崖边。

abstract.en: Imagine a wave taller than the boat.
abstract.cn: 想象一道比船还高的浪。

abstract.en: Think of applause that starts before thought.
abstract.cn: 想象先于思考爆发的掌声。

examples.en: The cathedral has an awesome silence.
examples.cn: 那座大教堂有一种令人肃然的静。

examples.en: They faced an awesome task.
examples.cn: 他们面对一项艰巨得令人敬畏的任务。

examples.en: Your new bike looks awesome.
examples.cn: 你的新自行车看起来太棒了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：awe「敬畏」+ -some「充满……的」——充满敬畏的，就是 awesome；口语里畏惧褪去，只剩「太棒了」。

root: 古诺斯语 agi「恐惧」入中古英语作 awe「敬畏」；1590 年代加 -some 成 awesome「令人敬畏的」，1960 年代美国口语又把它转为「极好的」。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are the same shock of scale: the grand thing that silences you, and the good thing that makes you shout.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项是同一种体量带来的震动：让你沉默的宏大之物，与让你喊出来的美好之物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: standing at a cliff edge with no words left
core.cn: 核心意象：站在崖边一时说不出话的那种震动

branches.en: A canyon rim that silences children.
branches.cn: 让孩子沉默的峡谷边缘。

branches.en: The force of the sea in a storm.
branches.cn: 风暴中海的力量。

branches.en: A concert called excellent.
branches.cn: 被称作极棒的音乐会。

branches.en: A new bike praised on sight.
branches.cn: 一眼就被夸的新自行车。

branches.en: Both name a shock, one sober and one glad.
branches.cn: 两者都指震动，一者肃然，一者欣喜。

intro.en: Awesome is awe plus -some; the same -some builds handsome and lonesome, while -ful gives the darker cousin awful.
intro.cn: awesome 是 awe 加 -some；同一 -some 还构成 handsome 与 lonesome，而 -ful 则给出走向阴暗的近亲 awful。

latinIntro.en: The base is Norse rather than Latin; Latin magnus, great, supplies magnificent beside it, and timere, to fear, gives timid.
latinIntro.cn: 词基属诺斯语而非拉丁语；旁边的拉丁语 magnus「大」提供 magnificent，timere「畏惧」产生 timid。

definition_zh: n. 男校友；男毕业生；（泛指）校友（复数 alumni）
definition_en: A male former student or graduate of a school, college or university; the plural alumni is also used for a mixed group.

scene: 校庆那天，返校的毕业生把礼堂坐满了。 Every alumnus received a letter from the new dean.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：从这所学校毕业的男性称 alumnus，复数是 alumni。新院长给每一位校友都寄了信。

senses.title: A male graduate
senses.definition: a man who formerly studied at a particular school, college or university
senses.definitionCN: 曾在某所学校、学院或大学就读的男性
senses.example: He is an alumnus of the engineering faculty.
senses.exampleCN: 他是工学院的校友。
senses.why: Latin alumnus meant a foster son, one nourished by a household, so the word carries the idea that the school fed your mind and you still owe it something.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 alumnus 意为养子，即被一个家庭养育的人，因此这个词带着「学校喂养过你的头脑、你仍欠它一份情」的意味。

senses.title: The mixed plural
senses.definition: used in the plural alumni for a body of former students of any gender
senses.definitionCN: 以复数 alumni 指任何性别构成的毕业生群体
senses.example: The alumni voted to fund a new laboratory.
senses.exampleCN: 校友们投票决定资助一间新实验室。
senses.why: Latin used the masculine plural for a mixed group, and English campus practice kept that rule, which is why alumni covers everyone while alumnae does not.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语用阳性复数指混合群体，英语校园沿用了这一规则，所以 alumni 涵盖所有人，而 alumnae 不涵盖。

intro.en: Alumnus is Latin for a foster son or pupil, from alere, to nourish. English kept the Latin plural alumni, and that plural is now the everyday word for a whole graduate body.
intro.cn: alumnus 在拉丁语中意为养子或学生，来自 alere「滋养」。英语保留了拉丁语复数 alumni，而这个复数如今就是「全体毕业生」的日常说法。

items.en: Alere meant to feed, nourish or bring up. From it come aliment, alimentary and alumnus, all built on the idea of being fed.
items.cn: alere 意为「喂养、滋养、养育」。由它产生 aliment、alimentary 与 alumnus，都建立在「被喂养」这个想法上。

items.en: Alumnus named a foster child raised in someone else house, and by extension a pupil raised by a teacher. The relation is one of care, not of blood.
items.cn: alumnus 指在别人家中养大的孩子，引申为由老师带大的学生。这种关系是养育关系，不是血缘关系。

items.en: The plural alumni covered a group of male or mixed pupils. English kept the form and widened it to the whole graduate body of an institution.
items.cn: 复数 alumni 指一群男性或混合性别的学生。英语保留该形式，并把它扩大到一所机构的全部毕业生。

items.en: American colleges organised alumni associations and alumni funds in the nineteenth century, which made the plural far more common than the singular.
items.cn: 美国高校在 19 世纪组织校友会与校友基金，这使复数形式远比单数常见。

items.en: Modern English uses alumnus for one man, alumni for a group, and the clipped alum in speech when gender does not matter.
items.cn: 现代英语用 alumnus 指一位男性，alumni 指一个群体，口语中在性别无关紧要时用缩写 alum。

note.en: The look-alike group sets the four Latin forms side by side; the near-meaning group lists other campus words for someone who has left.
note.cn: 形近组把四个拉丁语形式并排；近义组列出校园里其他表示「已离校者」的词。

normalIntro.en: Alumnus ends in -us, the Latin masculine ending, and its plural swaps -us for -i.

normal.en: The root means nourish: the school fed you, so you are its alumnus.
normal.cn: 词根意为「滋养」：学校喂养过你，所以你是它的 alumnus。

normal.en: Alumni is the plural you will meet most often in newsletters.
normal.cn: alumni 是你在校讯里最常见到的复数。

normal.en: Alumni can cover a mixed group; alumnae cannot.

normal.en: Alma mater is the nourishing mother, the same al- root.

abstract.en: Picture a grown man walking back into a small classroom.

abstract.en: Imagine a school sending a bill of gratitude instead of fees.

abstract.en: Think of a crowd of former pupils filling one hall.

examples.cn: 这所大学把每位校友都视为家庭的一员。

examples.en: Alumni from fifty years ago still meet each spring.
examples.cn: 五十年前的校友每年春天仍会聚会。

examples.en: He remained a generous alumnus long after retirement.

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are the same nourishing tie: one man who was fed here, and the whole body of people who were.

definition_zh: n. 阑尾炎（阑尾的炎症，急性发作常需手术切除）
definition_en: Inflammation of the appendix, the small pouch hanging off the large intestine; an acute attack causes worsening pain in the lower right abdomen and usually needs surgery.
core_image: 右下腹那一点突然绞紧，按下去更疼
scene: 半夜右下腹剧痛，急诊确诊为急性阑尾炎。 Acute appendicitis sent him to the operating theatre before dawn.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：appendicitis 指阑尾发炎，典型表现是右下腹持续加重的疼痛。

pos.zh: 阑尾炎

senses.title: Inflammation of the appendix
senses.definition: the medical condition in which the appendix becomes swollen and infected, named by the suffix -itis
senses.definitionCN: 阑尾肿胀发炎的病症，由后缀 -itis 标明为炎症
senses.example: Appendicitis is one of the commonest causes of abdominal surgery.
senses.exampleCN: 阑尾炎是腹部手术最常见的病因之一。
senses.why: The word is appendix plus -itis, so it names the disease by naming the part and then marking it as inflamed.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是 appendix 加 -itis，先点出部位，再标上「发炎」，病名就这样拼出来了。

senses.title: A surgical emergency
senses.definition: used of an acute attack that must be treated quickly, before the appendix bursts and infects the abdomen
senses.definitionCN: 指必须在阑尾穿孔感染腹腔之前尽快处理的急性发作
senses.example: The surgeon treated it as appendicitis and operated within two hours.
senses.exampleCN: 外科医生按阑尾炎处理，两小时内就动了手术。
senses.why: In hospital speech the word carries urgency: saying appendicitis is not just naming a disease but calling for an operation.
senses.whyCN: 在医院语境里这个词带着紧迫感：说 appendicitis 不只是报病名，而是在要求立刻手术。

intro.en: Appendicitis is appendix plus the inflammation suffix -itis. Appendix comes from Latin appendere, to hang beside, from ad- and pendere, to hang.
intro.cn: appendicitis 是 appendix 加炎症后缀 -itis。appendix 来自拉丁语 appendere「挂在旁边」，由 ad- 与 pendere「悬挂」构成。

items.en: Latin pendere meant to hang, and also to weigh, since scales hang. It gives pendant, pendulum, depend and suspend.
items.cn: 拉丁语 pendere 意为「悬挂」，也指「称重」，因为天平是挂着的。它产生 pendant、pendulum、depend 与 suspend。

items.en: With ad-, to, it became appendere, to hang something beside a main thing, so the added part is secondary.
items.cn: 加上 ad-「向」成为 appendere「把某物挂在主体旁边」，因此附加的部分是次要的。

items.en: The noun appendix meant an appendage, and English used it for a supplement at the end of a book.
items.cn: 名词 appendix 意为「附属物」，英语用它指书末的附录。

items.en: Anatomy kept appendix for the small blind pouch hanging off the caecum, a literal appendage of the gut.
items.cn: 解剖学把 appendix 留给挂在盲肠上的那条小盲管，它字面上就是肠子的附属物。

items.en: Greek -itis was a feminine adjective ending agreeing with nosos, disease; medicine reanalysed it as inflammation.
items.cn: 希腊语 -itis 本是与 nosos「疾病」呼应的阴性形容词词尾，医学把它重新理解为「炎症」。

items.en: Reginald Fitz named the condition appendicitis in 1886 and argued for early surgery, which saved many lives.
items.cn: 1886 年 Reginald Fitz 把这一病症命名为 appendicitis，并主张早期手术，救了许多人的命。

note.en: The look-alike group separates the organ appendix from the disease, and shows other -itis names; the near-meaning group lists related abdominal conditions.
note.cn: 形近组把器官 appendix 与疾病区分开，并展示其他 -itis 病名；近义组列出相关的腹部病症。

normalIntro.en: Appendicitis is appendix plus -itis: the little hanging pouch has become inflamed.
normalIntro.cn: appendicitis 就是 appendix 加 -itis：那条挂着的小盲管发炎了。

normal.en: The suffix -itis always marks inflammation.
normal.cn: 后缀 -itis 一律表示炎症。

normal.en: Appendix is the part; appendicitis is the disease.
normal.cn: appendix 是部位，appendicitis 是疾病。

normal.en: It is uncountable: say appendicitis, not an appendicitis.
normal.cn: 它不可数：说 appendicitis，不说 an appendicitis。

normal.en: The stress falls on -ci-, /ˈsaɪ/, not on the start.
normal.cn: 重音落在 -ci- 上，读 /ˈsaɪ/，不在词首。

normal.en: The operation is an appendectomy, with -ectomy for removal.
normal.cn: 手术叫 appendectomy，-ectomy 表示切除。

abstract.en: Picture a small pouch swelling on the side of a pipe.
abstract.cn: 想象管道侧面一个小囊袋肿了起来。

abstract.en: Imagine pain moving from the navel to the lower right.
abstract.cn: 想象疼痛从肚脐移到右下腹。

abstract.en: Think of a clock: every hour of delay raises the risk.
abstract.cn: 想象一只钟：每延误一小时，风险就升一分。

examples.en: The doctor ruled out appendicitis after a scan.
examples.cn: 扫描之后，医生排除了阑尾炎。

examples.en: Untreated appendicitis can lead to peritonitis.
examples.cn: 阑尾炎不治疗可能引发腹膜炎。

examples.en: She was in hospital for a week after appendicitis.
examples.cn: 阑尾炎之后她住院一周。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：append「附加」+ ix + itis「炎」——挂在肠子旁边那截小尾巴发炎了，就是阑尾炎 appendicitis。

root: 拉丁语 pendere「悬挂」加 ad-「向」成 appendere「挂在旁边」，名词 appendix「附属物」被解剖学用来指阑尾；再加希腊炎症后缀 -itis，1886 年构成病名 appendicitis。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are one inflamed pouch: the disease as a named condition, and the same disease as an emergency that must be operated on.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项是同一条发炎的盲管：作为病名的疾病，以及作为必须立刻手术的急症的同一疾病。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one spot in the lower right belly gripping tight, worse when pressed
core.cn: 核心意象：右下腹那一点突然绞紧，按下去更疼

branches.en: A pouch swollen beside the gut.
branches.cn: 肠子旁边肿起来的盲管。

branches.en: A named cause of belly surgery.
branches.cn: 腹部手术的一个明确病因。

branches.en: Pain shifting to the lower right.
branches.cn: 转移到右下腹的疼痛。

branches.en: Surgery within two hours of arrival.
branches.cn: 到院两小时内就手术。

branches.en: Both are the same inflamed appendage.
branches.cn: 两者都是同一条发炎的附属盲管。

intro.en: Appendicitis joins the prefix ap-, the hang root pend- and the disease suffix -itis, a pattern shared by many medical names.
intro.cn: appendicitis 拼合了前缀 ap-、「悬挂」词根 pend- 与疾病后缀 -itis，这是许多医学病名共用的构词模式。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is pendere, appendere and appendix; the suffix -itis is Greek but arrived through medical Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语层次是 pendere、appendere 与 appendix；后缀 -itis 来自希腊语，但经医学拉丁语传入。

latinEntries.exampleCN: pendere 产生 pendant 与 depend。
appendix 被用来命名肠道盲管。
itis 把 arthritis 标为炎症。

definition_zh: 炼金术士；（比喻）点石成金的人
definition_en: a person who practised alchemy, trying to turn base metals into gold; figuratively, someone who turns ordinary material into something valuable
core_image: 守着炉子想把铅变成金的那个人
scene: 他守着一炉黑灰熬了半辈子，只想把铅变成金子。 The alchemist kept his furnace burning all night.
sceneCN: 这里 alchemist 是「炼金术士」（第 1 个义项：试图把贱金属变成黄金的古代化学实践者）；句意为这位炼金术士让炉子整夜烧着。核心画面是守着炉子想把铅变成金的那个人。

pos.zh: 炼金术士；点石成金的人

derivatives.zh: 去掉 -ist 的学科名，义为「炼金术」
加 -ical 构成，义为「炼金术的」
加 -ize 构成，义为「使嬗变；点化」

senses.title: One who practised alchemy
senses.definition: a person who tried to turn base metals into gold and to find a universal medicine, working before modern chemistry existed
senses.definitionCN: 试图把贱金属变成黄金并寻找万能药的人，其活动早于现代化学的出现
senses.example: The alchemist recorded every failure in a coded notebook.
senses.exampleCN: 这位炼金术士把每次失败都记在一本用暗语写的笔记里。
senses.why: Alchemy came from Arabic al-kimiya, the art of substances, and -ist marks the person who practises an art, so alchemist is the practiser of that art.
senses.whyCN: alchemy 来自阿拉伯语 al-kimiya「物质的技艺」，-ist 表示从事某种技艺的人，所以 alchemist 就是这门技艺的实践者。

senses.title: A worker of modern transformations
senses.definition: someone praised for turning ordinary material into something valuable, used figuratively of chefs, coaches and producers
senses.definitionCN: 因把普通材料变成有价值的东西而受称赞的人，比喻用于厨师、教练与制作人
senses.example: The producer is an alchemist who turns demos into hits.
senses.exampleCN: 这位制作人是点石成金的人，把小样变成热门歌曲。
senses.why: The furnace is gone but the transformation stays: we borrow the old figure whenever cheap input becomes precious output.
senses.whyCN: 炉子不见了，但「转化」留了下来：每当廉价投入变成珍贵产出，我们就借用这个古老形象。

intro.en: Alchemist travelled a long road: Greek chymeia, the art of pouring and mixing, prefixed by Arabic al-, the, then split by the suffix -ist into a person.
intro.cn: alchemist 走过一条长路：希腊语 chymeia「倾倒与混合的技艺」，加上阿拉伯语冠词 al-，再由后缀 -ist 分出「人」。

items.en: Greek chymeia meant the art of pouring and fusing metals, from chein, to pour.
items.cn: 希腊语 chymeia 指倾倒与熔合金属的技艺，源自 chein「倾倒」。

items.en: Arabic added the article al- to give al-kimiya, and the word entered Europe through translations made in Spain.
items.cn: 阿拉伯语加上冠词 al- 构成 al-kimiya，该词经西班牙的译本传入欧洲。

items.en: Scholarly Latin alchimia named the whole pursuit of transmutation and the elixir of life.
items.cn: 学术拉丁语 alchimia 指嬗变与长生药的全部追求。

items.en: Old French alquimiste added an agent ending to name the person practising the art.
items.cn: 古法语 alquimiste 加上表示行为者的词尾，指从事该技艺的人。

items.en: Middle English took the word in the fourteenth century, and Chaucer mocked such figures in his tales of the canon yeoman.
items.cn: 中古英语在十四世纪借入该词，乔叟在教士侍从的故事中嘲讽过这类人物。

items.en: Today alchemist is historical in its literal sense and admiring in its figurative one, while chemistry kept the science.
items.cn: 如今 alchemist 的字面义属历史，比喻义带赞赏，而 chemistry 保留了科学那一支。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the alchem- family; the near-meaning group lists other words for someone who transforms or pretends to.
note.cn: 形近组保留 alchem- 词族；近义组列出其他表示「转化者或自称转化者」的词。

entries.definitionCN: 炼金术中假想的万能溶剂。

entries.definition: A person who performs apparent wonders.
