normalIntro.en: Alchemist is alchemy plus -ist: the person who does alchemy, the one at the furnace.
normalIntro.cn: alchemist 就是 alchemy 加 -ist：做炼金术的那个人，守在炉子边的人。

normal.en: -ist marks a practiser: chemist, artist and alchemist all name the person, not the subject.
normal.cn: -ist 表示从事者：chemist、artist、alchemist 都指人，不指学科。

normal.en: Alchemy is the art; alchemist is the artist. Drop -ist and you drop the person.
normal.cn: alchemy 是技艺，alchemist 是艺人。去掉 -ist 就去掉了人。

normal.en: The al- is the Arabic article the, the same al- you see in alcohol and algebra.
normal.cn: 这个 al- 是阿拉伯语冠词，与 alcohol、algebra 中的 al- 相同。

normal.en: Figuratively an alchemist turns cheap into precious, so praise a chef with it.
normal.cn: 比喻义上 alchemist 把廉价变珍贵，所以可以用它夸厨师。

normal.en: Do not confuse alchemist with chemist: one sought gold, the other studies matter.
normal.cn: 别把 alchemist 与 chemist 混淆：一个求黄金，一个研究物质。

abstract.en: Picture a man asleep beside a furnace that has burned for forty years.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人守在烧了四十年的炉子旁睡着。

abstract.en: Imagine a lead coin dropped into a pot and lifted out as gold.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚铅币放进锅里，捞出来时成了金币。

abstract.en: Think of a kitchen where leftovers come out as a banquet.
abstract.cn: 想象一间厨房，剩菜进去，宴席出来。

examples.en: The alchemist hid his recipes from rival workshops.
examples.cn: 这位炼金术士把配方藏起来，不让对手作坊看到。

examples.en: She called the editor an alchemist of forgotten manuscripts.
examples.cn: 她称这位编辑是被遗忘手稿的点金者。

examples.en: Every alchemist dreamed of the philosopher's stone.
examples.cn: 每个炼金术士都梦想得到哲人石。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「阿尔凯米斯特」——阿尔（al）凯米（chemy）斯特（ist）：守着炉子的那个人，就是炼金术士。

root: 希腊语 chymeia「倾倒与熔合金属的技艺」加阿拉伯语冠词 al- 构成 al-kimiya，经中世纪拉丁语 alchimia 与古法语 alquimiste 进入英语，加表示行为者的 -ist 构成 alchemist，字面即「从事炼金术的人」。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses name a transformer: the literal one worked a furnace to change metal, and the figurative one works a kitchen, a studio or a training ground to change value.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项都指「转化者」：字面义守着炉子改变金属，比喻义在厨房、录音室或训练场上改变价值。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person at the furnace turning lead into gold
core.cn: 核心意象：守在炉边把铅变成金的人

branches.en: A coded notebook of failed trials.
branches.cn: 一本记满失败试验的暗语笔记。

branches.en: A search for the elixir of life.
branches.cn: 对长生药的寻找。

branches.en: A chef turning scraps into a dish.
branches.cn: 厨师把边角料做成一道菜。

branches.en: A coach turning a weak side into winners.
branches.cn: 教练把弱队带成冠军。

branches.en: Both turn the cheap into the precious.
branches.cn: 两者都把廉价变成珍贵。

intro.en: Alchemist keeps three visible layers: the Arabic article al-, the Greek root chem- for fusing, and the agent suffix -ist.
intro.cn: alchemist 保留三个可见层次：阿拉伯语冠词 al-、表示熔合的希腊词根 chem-，以及表示行为者的后缀 -ist。

latinIntro.en: The word reached Latin as alchimia from Arabic al-kimiya, itself built on Greek chymeia.
latinIntro.cn: 该词以 alchimia 的形式从阿拉伯语 al-kimiya 进入拉丁语，而 al-kimiya 又建立在希腊语 chymeia 之上。

latinEntries.example: Alchimia carried the Arabic word into Latin.
latinEntries.exampleCN: alchimia 把阿拉伯语词带入拉丁语。

latinEntries.example: Chymeia comes from chein, to pour.
The French form gave English its ending.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 法语形式为英语提供了词尾。

definition_zh: 密封的；不透气的；（论点、不在场证明）无懈可击的
definition_en: closed so tightly that no air can enter or escape; figuratively, so carefully constructed that no flaw or objection can get in
core_image: 连一丝空气都挤不进去的封口
scene: 这罐咖啡豆开封后必须拧紧，否则香气几天就散了。 An airtight jar keeps the beans fresh.
sceneCN: 这里 airtight 是「密封的」（第 1 个义项：封得极紧、空气进不出）；句意为密封罐能让咖啡豆保持新鲜。核心画面是连一丝空气都挤不进去的封口。

pos.zh: 密封的；不透气的；无懈可击的

collocations.zh: 无懈可击的不在场证明

derivatives.zh: 加 -ly 构成，义为「密封地；严密地」
加 -ness 构成，义为「密封性；严密性」
去掉 air- 的部分，义为「紧的；严密的」

senses.title: Letting no air in or out
senses.definition: closed so tightly that no air can enter or escape, used of containers, seals and rooms
senses.definitionCN: 封得极紧，空气既进不去也出不来，用于容器、封口与房间
senses.example: Store the flour in an airtight container.
senses.exampleCN: 把面粉存放在密封容器里。
senses.why: Air plus tight is literal: the seal is tight against air itself, so nothing gaseous can pass either way.
senses.whyCN: air 加 tight 是字面组合：封口对空气本身都是紧的，所以任何气体双向都过不去。

senses.title: Leaving no gap for doubt
senses.titleCN: 无懈可击的；滴水不漏的
senses.definition: so carefully constructed that no flaw or objection can get in, used of arguments, alibis and security
senses.definitionCN: 构造得极其严密，任何漏洞或反驳都钻不进来，用于论点、不在场证明与安保
senses.example: Her alibi was airtight, so the police let her go.
senses.exampleCN: 她的不在场证明无懈可击，警方于是放了她。
senses.why: The same seal is imagined around a claim: if no air gets in, no doubt gets in either, and the argument holds.
senses.whyCN: 同一道封口被想象在某个说法周围：空气进不来，怀疑也进不来，论点就站得住。

intro.en: Airtight is a transparent English compound: air plus tight, first of physical seals and later of anything that admits no gap.
intro.cn: airtight 是一个透明的英语复合词：air 加 tight，先指实物封口，后来指任何不留缝隙的东西。

items.en: Greek aer meant air, and it reached English as air through Latin and Old French.
items.cn: 希腊语 aer 意为空气，经拉丁语与古法语进入英语成为 air。

items.en: Old Norse thettr meant close or watertight, and Middle English took it as thight, later tight.
items.cn: 古挪威语 thettr 意为紧密、不透水，中古英语借作 thight，后来成为 tight。

items.en: By the fifteenth century tight meant firmly fixed or leaving no gap, used of knots and seals.
items.cn: 到十五世纪，tight 意为固定得牢或不留缝隙，用于绳结与封口。

items.en: English joined air to tight in the seventeenth century, first written with a hyphen, of vessels that held air.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪把 air 与 tight 拼合，最初带连字符，指能保住空气的容器。

items.en: The hyphen dropped and the word gained a figurative sense in the nineteenth century, of alibis and reasoning.
items.cn: 连字符脱落，该词在十九世纪获得比喻义，用于不在场证明与推理。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the -tight compounds; the near-meaning group lists other words for sealed or flawless.
note.cn: 形近组保留 -tight 复合词；近义组列出其他表示「密封」或「无漏洞」的词。

entries.definition: Letting no water through; leaving no doubt.
Firmly fixed, leaving little space.
entries.definitionCN: 固定得牢，几乎不留空隙。

entries.definition: The quality of being sealed against air.
Anxious and unable to relax.
Closed so that nothing can pass in or out.
entries.definitionCN: 封住使任何东西都进不出。

entries.definition: Completely sealed, especially against air.
entries.definitionCN: 完全密封的，尤指对空气。

entries.definition: Without any defect or mistake.
Impossible to attack or dispute.

normalIntro.en: Airtight is air plus tight: tight against air, and by extension tight against doubt.
normalIntro.cn: airtight 就是 air 加 tight：对空气是紧的，引申为对怀疑也是紧的。

normal.en: Watertight and airtight are built the same way: name what must not get through.
normal.cn: watertight 与 airtight 构词方式相同：说出不能让什么东西通过。

normal.en: An airtight alibi lets no doubt in, just as an airtight jar lets no air in.
normal.cn: 无懈可击的不在场证明不让怀疑进来，正如密封罐不让空气进来。

normal.en: It is usually placed before a noun: an airtight case, an airtight seal.
normal.cn: 它通常放在名词前：an airtight case、an airtight seal。

normal.en: The older spelling air-tight means exactly the same thing.
normal.cn: 较早的拼写 air-tight 意思完全相同。

normal.en: Do not say very airtight in formal writing; prefer completely airtight.
normal.cn: 正式写作中不说 very airtight，宜用 completely airtight。

abstract.en: Picture a jar whose lid has no seam at all.
abstract.cn: 想象一只罐子，盖子上完全没有接缝。

abstract.en: Imagine an argument wrapped in glass so no objection can reach it.
abstract.cn: 想象一个论点被玻璃包住，任何反驳都碰不到它。

abstract.en: Think of a story with every hole already plugged.
abstract.cn: 想象一个故事，每个漏洞都已被堵上。

examples.en: The lid forms an airtight seal when you press it down.
examples.cn: 按下盖子时会形成密封。

examples.en: Prosecutors need an airtight case before going to trial.
examples.cn: 检方在开庭前需要一个无懈可击的案子。

examples.en: Keep the vaccine in airtight packaging.
examples.cn: 把疫苗保存在密封包装中。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「艾尔太特」——艾尔（air）是气，太特（tight）是紧：气都挤不进去，就是密封的、无懈可击的。

root: air 源自希腊语 aer「空气」，tight 源自古挪威语 thettr「紧密、不透水」经中古英语 thight 演变而来；十七世纪两者拼合为 air-tight，指不透气，十九世纪引申为「无懈可击」。

sensesIntro.en: One seal is described twice: physically it stops air, figuratively it stops doubt, and in both cases the point is that nothing unwanted gets through.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一道封口被描述了两次：实物层面挡住空气，比喻层面挡住怀疑，两者的要点都是「不让任何不想要的东西通过」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a seal that lets nothing through
core.cn: 核心意象：一道什么都不让过的封口

branches.en: A jar lid with no gap.
branches.cn: 没有缝隙的罐盖。

branches.en: A room sealed against fumes.
branches.cn: 封住不让烟气进入的房间。

branches.en: An alibi with every minute accounted for.
branches.cn: 每分钟都有交代的不在场证明。

branches.en: A contract with no loophole.
branches.cn: 没有漏洞的合同。

branches.en: Both refuse any unwanted entry.
branches.cn: 两者都拒绝任何不想要的进入。

intro.en: Airtight belongs to the -tight family, where the first element names what must be kept out and tight supplies the idea of a firm seal.
intro.cn: airtight 属于 -tight 词族：前一个成分说明要挡住什么，tight 提供「封得紧」的想法。

latinIntro.en: Only air has a classical source, Greek aer through Latin aer; tight came from Old Norse, so the Latin layer is thin.
latinIntro.cn: 只有 air 有古典来源，即希腊语 aer 经拉丁语 aer；tight 来自古挪威语，所以拉丁语层次很薄。

definition_zh: n. 动画（制作）；动画片；生气；活力
definition_en: The technique of making still images appear to move, a film made that way, or the quality of being lively and full of spirit.
core_image: 一张张静止的画被喂进一口气，动起来
scene: 这部片子用了三年，每一帧都是手绘的。 The animation took three years to finish.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：把逐张手绘的静止画面连续播放，让画面动起来，这门技术与成品都叫 animation。

pos.zh: 动画；动画片；活力

senses.title: The technique and the film
senses.definition: the method of photographing successive drawings or frames so that they appear to move, and the film produced
senses.definitionCN: 把连续的图画或帧逐一拍摄使其看似运动的方法，以及由此制成的影片
senses.example: The studio released two animations in one year.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工作室一年推出了两部动画片。
senses.why: Latin anima means breath or soul, so animation is literally the act of breathing life into something still.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 anima 意为「气息、灵魂」，所以 animation 字面上就是给静止之物吹进一口气的动作。

senses.title: Liveliness of manner
senses.definition: the quality of being energetic and expressive in speech or movement
senses.definitionCN: 言语或动作中精力充沛、富于表现力的特质
senses.example: She told the story with great animation.
senses.exampleCN: 她讲这个故事时眉飞色舞。
senses.why: The same breath is meant, but now in a person: a face or voice that has been given life rather than left flat.
senses.whyCN: 所指的仍是同一口气，只是现在发生在人身上：一张脸或一副嗓音被赋予了生气，而不是平淡无神。

senses.title: The act of giving life
senses.definition: the act of making something live or move, the oldest and most literal sense
senses.definitionCN: 使某物活起来或动起来的行为，是最古老也最字面的义项
senses.example: The animation of the puppet required twelve operators.
senses.exampleCN: 让这具木偶动起来需要十二名操作者。
senses.why: This is the base sense from which both the film technique and the lively manner are extensions.
senses.whyCN: 这是基础义，电影技术与生动神情两个义项都是它的延伸。

intro.en: Animation is Latin animatio, from animare, to give breath to, from anima, breath or soul. The film sense is only about a century old; the older sense is simply life.
intro.cn: animation 来自拉丁语 animatio，出自 animare「赋予气息」，而 animare 又来自 anima「气息、灵魂」。电影义只有约一百年历史；更早的义项就是「生命」。

items.en: Latin anima meant breath, air, and then the soul as the breath of life. The same root gives animal and animate.
items.cn: 拉丁语 anima 意为「气息、空气」，进而指作为生命之息的灵魂。同一词根产生 animal 与 animate。

items.en: Animare meant to fill with breath, to enliven, and also to give a soul to. The verb keeps the physical act of blowing life in.
items.cn: animare 意为「充入气息、使有生气」，也指「赋予灵魂」。这个动词保留了「吹进生命」的身体动作。

items.en: Animatio was the noun of action, an enlivening. It entered English in the sixteenth century for the act of giving life.
items.cn: animatio 是动作名词，意为「赋予生气」。它在 16 世纪进入英语，指赋予生命这一行为。

items.en: The cinematic sense dates from the early twentieth century, when successive drawings were photographed to create movement.
items.cn: 电影义始于 20 世纪初，当时人们把连续的图画逐张拍摄以制造运动感。

items.en: Modern English keeps all three uses: the industry, the lively manner, and the literal giving of life, with animate and animator alongside.
items.cn: 现代英语保留三种用法：产业、生动神情与字面的赋予生命，并配有 animate 与 animator。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the anima family including animus, which means hostility; the near-meaning group lists words for liveliness and cartoons.
note.cn: 形近组保留 anima 词族，包括意为「敌意」的 animus；近义组列出表示活力与卡通的词。

entries.definition: To give life or movement to.
Full of life; made as a cartoon.
entries.definitionCN: 充满生气的；制成动画的。

entries.definition: A person who makes animation.
Hostility or a guiding intention.
The quality of being full of energy.
Strong active energy.
An animated film or a comic drawing.
Lively and animated spirit.

normalIntro.en: Animation is anima plus -tion: breath put into something, whether a drawing or a face.
normalIntro.cn: animation 就是 anima 加 -tion：把气息放进某物，无论那是一张画还是一张脸。

normal.en: Anima means breath, so animation is breathing life in.
normal.cn: anima 意为「气息」，所以 animation 就是吹进生命。

normal.en: Uncountable for the craft, countable for films: two animations.
normal.cn: 指技艺时不可数，指影片时可数：two animations。

normal.en: With animation describes how someone speaks, not what they say.
normal.cn: with animation 描述说话的方式，而不是内容。

normal.en: Do not confuse animus, hostility, with anima, breath.
normal.cn: 别把 animus「敌意」与 anima「气息」混淆。

normal.en: The person is an animator; the adjective is animated.
normal.cn: 从业者是 animator，形容词是 animated。

abstract.en: Picture a stack of drawings flicked into movement.
abstract.cn: 想象一叠画被快速翻动成运动。

abstract.en: Imagine a flat face suddenly lighting up.
abstract.cn: 想象一张平淡的脸忽然亮起来。

abstract.en: Think of a puppet taking its first breath.
abstract.cn: 想象一具木偶吸进第一口气。

examples.en: The animation was drawn entirely by hand.
examples.cn: 这部动画完全由手绘完成。

examples.en: He spoke with an animation that filled the room.
examples.cn: 他讲得眉飞色舞，感染了整个房间。

examples.en: The animation of the model took six months.
examples.cn: 让这个模型动起来花了六个月。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「爱你妹神」——爱你（ani）妹（ma）神（tion）：给画吹一口「神气」，画就活了，就是动画；人有了这股神气就是活力。

root: 拉丁语 anima「气息、灵魂」生出 animare「赋予气息」，动作名词 animatio 入英语为 animation，本义「赋予生命」，引申为动画技术与生动神情。

sensesIntro.en: All three senses are one breath: life given to a drawing, life showing in a face, and the plain act of giving life.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项是同一口气：吹进画里的生命、显现在脸上的生气，以及「赋予生命」这个本义动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: still drawings fed one breath and starting to move
core.cn: 核心意象：静止的画被喂进一口气后动起来

branches.en: Twelve frames for one second of film.
branches.cn: 一秒影片用十二帧。

branches.en: A studio of hand-drawn features.
branches.cn: 一间手绘长片的工作室。

branches.en: A storyteller with moving hands.
branches.cn: 一个双手不停比划的讲故事者。

branches.en: Twelve operators behind one puppet.
branches.cn: 一具木偶背后的十二名操作者。

branches.en: All three are breath given to something still.
branches.cn: 三者都是把气息给静止之物。

intro.en: Animation is anima plus -ate plus -ion, and the breath root also builds animal, animate and animus.
intro.cn: animation 是 anima 加 -ate 加 -ion，这个「气息」词根还构成 animal、animate 与 animus。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is anima, breath, and animare, to enliven; animatio is the regular noun of action built on that verb.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语层次是 anima「气息」与 animare「使有生气」；animatio 是建立在该动词上的规则动作名词。

latinEntries.example: Anima is the root of the family.
Animatio is the noun of action.

definition_zh: adj. 轶事的；基于个别传闻的（非系统证据）
definition_en: Based on personal accounts or isolated stories rather than on systematic study or measurement.
core_image: 几个人讲的故事，凑不出一张统计图
scene: 他说这药有效，可依据只是邻居的几句话。 The evidence for the remedy is purely anecdotal.
sceneCN: 第 2 个义项：这里说的不是「趣闻」，而是证据性质——只有个别口述，没有系统测量，所以是传闻性证据。

pos.zh: 轶事的；传闻性的

forms.label: 无 -er/-est 形式（多音节形容词，用 more/most）

senses.title: Of the nature of a short story
senses.definition: consisting of short, entertaining accounts of particular incidents
senses.definitionCN: 由对个别事件的简短有趣叙述构成的
senses.example: His memoir is warm and anecdotal rather than analytical.
senses.exampleCN: 他的回忆录温暖而多轶事，而非分析性的。
senses.why: The noun anecdote once meant an unpublished secret account, so the adjective still carries the sense of a private story told aloud.
senses.whyCN: 名词 anecdote 原指未公开的秘闻，所以这个形容词仍带着「私下讲出来的故事」这层意味。

senses.title: Of evidence that is not systematic
senses.definition: resting on isolated reports rather than on controlled measurement, and therefore weak as proof
senses.definitionCN: 依据零散口述而非受控测量，因而作为证明力度不足
senses.example: Anecdotal evidence cannot establish a causal link.
senses.exampleCN: 传闻性证据无法确立因果关系。
senses.why: In research writing the word is a warning label: the stories may be true, but they were not collected in a way that lets you generalise.
senses.whyCN: 在研究写作中这个词是一个警示标签：那些故事也许是真的，但收集方式不足以让你推广结论。

intro.en: Anecdotal is the adjective of anecdote, from Greek anekdota, things not published, from an-, not, and ekdotos, given out. Procopius used it for his secret history of Justinian.
intro.cn: anecdotal 是 anecdote 的形容词，anecdote 来自希腊语 anekdota「未公开之事」，由 an-「不」与 ekdotos「发布出去的」构成。普罗科匹乌斯用它称呼自己那部关于查士丁尼的秘史。

items.en: Greek an- means not or without before a vowel, the same prefix seen in anaerobic and anarchy.
items.cn: 希腊语 an- 在元音前意为「不、没有」，与 anaerobic、anarchy 中的前缀相同。

items.en: Greek ekdotos meant given out or published, from ekdidonai, to give out. The core image is handing a text over to the public.
items.cn: 希腊语 ekdotos 意为「发布出去的、出版的」，来自 ekdidonai「给出、发布」。核心意象是把一份文本交到公众手上。

items.en: Anekdota therefore meant unpublished things. Procopius gave that title to the secret account he kept back from official publication.
items.cn: 因此 anekdota 意为「未公开之事」。普罗科匹乌斯把这个名字给了他那部未正式公开的秘史。

items.en: French anecdote and then English anecdote shifted the sense from a secret account to a short entertaining story about a real incident.
items.cn: 法语 anecdote 与随后的英语 anecdote 把含义从「秘闻」转为「关于真实事件的简短有趣故事」。

items.en: Anecdotal is built with -al, and in modern research writing it labels evidence that rests on stories rather than measurement.
items.cn: anecdotal 用 -al 构成，在现代研究写作中用来标注依据故事而非测量的证据。

note.en: The look-alike group warns against antidotal, about antidotes; the near-meaning group lists other words for unmeasured claims.
note.cn: 形近组提醒别与 antidotal「解毒剂的」混淆；近义组列出其他表示未经测量的说法的词。

entries.definition: A short amusing story about a real incident.
entries.definitionCN: 关于真实事件的简短有趣故事。

entries.definition: According to isolated reports.
Relating to a remedy against poison.
Based on systematic breakdown.
Information received from others, not witnessed.
entries.definitionCN: 从他人处听来而非亲见的信息。

entries.definition: Not yet checked for truth.
Based on personal feeling rather than fact.
entries.definitionCN: 基于个人感受而非事实的。

entries.definition: Not following formal procedure.

normalIntro.en: Anecdotal is an- plus ekdotos: not published, so a private story rather than a public dataset.
normalIntro.cn: anecdotal 就是 an- 加 ekdotos：未公开的，所以是私下的故事，而不是公开的数据集。

normal.en: The fixed phrase is anecdotal evidence, and it is a caution, not praise.
normal.cn: 固定搭配是 anecdotal evidence，它是警示而非褒奖。

normal.en: Anecdotally is common in speech: anecdotally, the shop is always full.
normal.cn: anecdotally 在口语中常见：据大家说，那家店总是满的。

normal.en: Do not confuse anecdotal with antidotal, about poisons.
normal.cn: 别把 anecdotal 与 antidotal「关于解毒」混淆。

normal.en: The noun is anecdote, stressed on the first syllable.
normal.cn: 名词是 anecdote，重音在第一音节。

normal.en: Anecdotal is not the opposite of true; it is the opposite of systematic.
normal.cn: anecdotal 不是「真实」的反面，而是「系统」的反面。

abstract.en: Picture three neighbours telling three different stories.
abstract.cn: 想象三个邻居讲着三个不同的故事。

abstract.en: Imagine a chart with only one dot on it.
abstract.cn: 想象一张只画了一个点的图表。

abstract.en: Think of a drawer of unpublished letters.
abstract.cn: 想象一抽屉从未公开的信。

examples.en: The claim rests on anecdotal evidence alone.
examples.cn: 这一说法仅依据传闻性证据。

examples.en: Anecdotally, the new timetable has helped.
examples.cn: 据大家反映，新时间表有帮助。

examples.en: The book is anecdotal rather than statistical.
examples.cn: 这本书多轶事而少统计。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「安尼克多头」——安（an）尼（ec）克（d）多头（otal）：一个人一个说法，多头口述凑不成数据，就是传闻性的。

root: 希腊语 an-「不」+ ekdotos「发布出去的」构成 anekdota「未公开之事」，经法语 anecdote 转为「轶事」，英语加 -al 成 anecdotal，引申指依据零散口述的证据。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are one kind of private account: a short entertaining story, and the same story used as weak evidence.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项是同一种私下叙述：一段简短有趣的故事，以及同一段故事被当作力度不足的证据。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a few stories that cannot add up to a chart
core.cn: 核心意象：几个故事凑不出一张统计图

branches.en: A memoir full of small incidents.
branches.cn: 一部满是小事的回忆录。

branches.en: A dinner table of amusing tales.
branches.cn: 一桌讲趣闻的晚餐。

branches.en: One patient who says the pill worked.
branches.cn: 一位说服了药的患者。

branches.en: A claim with no sample behind it.
branches.cn: 一个背后没有样本的说法。

branches.en: Both are single accounts, not datasets.
branches.cn: 两者都是单个叙述，不是数据集。

intro.en: Anecdotal is an- plus the give-out root dot- plus -al, and the same dot- builds antidote and dose.
intro.cn: anecdotal 是 an- 加「给出」词根 dot- 加 -al，同一个 dot- 还构成 antidote 与 dose。

latinIntro.en: The pieces are Greek an- and ekdotos, from ekdidonai, to give out; Latin passed the word on through French anecdote.
latinIntro.cn: 部件是希腊语 an- 与 ekdotos，后者来自 ekdidonai「给出」；该词经法语 anecdote 传入。

latinEntries.exampleCN: anekdota 是那部秘史的名字。
ekdidonai 是 ekdotos 的来源。

definition_zh: 祖先的；祖传的；与先人有关的；（物种或语言）原始类型的
definition_en: relating to ancestors, inherited from them, or marking an early form from which later ones developed
core_image: 一条向身后延伸的家族链，链的最前端站着先人；今天的一切都从那里传来
scene: 清明时，一家人回到祖屋，擦亮刻着先人名字的木牌，摆上供品。 At Qingming, the family returns to the old house, polishes the wooden tablets with the names of the dead and lays out offerings in the ancestral hall.
sceneCN: 这里 ancestral 是「祖先祭祀的、先人的」（第 5 个义项：祭祀与纪念先人的）；句意：清明时一家人回到祖屋，在祖先祠堂里擦亮刻有先人名字的木牌并摆上供品。场景要点：祖屋的木门、刻名字的牌位、供桌、香炉、擦拭牌位的手。

pos.zh: 祖先的；祖传的；原始类型的

forms.label: 比较级（更多用 more 构成）
最高级（更多用 most 构成）

derivatives.zh: 在祖先方面；按祖先的方式
祖先的（ancestral 的替代形式）

senses.title: Belonging to the people before you
senses.titleCN: 属于先人的：指向家族中的前人
senses.definition: relating to the ancestors from whom a person or family is descended
senses.definitionCN: 与某个人或家族所出自的先人有关的
senses.example: A faded ancestral portrait hangs above the fireplace.
senses.exampleCN: 壁炉上方挂着一幅褪色的先人画像。
senses.why: The suffix -al changes the concrete noun ancestor ('a forebear') into a relation word: it does not name the person but marks anything that points back to that person.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -al 把具体名词 ancestor（先人）变成关系形容词：它不指那个人，而是标记任何指向那个人的事物。

senses.title: Inherited through the family line
senses.definition: received from ancestors, especially as property, traits, or rights
senses.definitionCN: 从先人那里继承而来的，尤指财产、特征或权利
senses.example: The orchard came with an ancestral right to draw water from the stream.
senses.exampleCN: 这座果园附带一项从溪中取水的祖传权利。
senses.why: Inheritance is how the family chain continues materially: what the earlier generation held passes to the later one, so 'of ancestors' comes to mean 'handed down from them'.
senses.whyCN: 继承是家族链在物质上延续的方式：上一代握有的东西传给下一代，于是“属于先人的”引申为“由先人传下的”。

senses.title: Marking the original home
senses.definition: describing the place where a family or people originated and to which it still traces itself
senses.definitionCN: 描述某个家族或民族发源、并且至今仍以之为归属的地方
senses.example: Her ancestral village sits at the end of a narrow valley.
senses.exampleCN: 她的祖籍村落在一条狭窄山谷的尽头。
senses.why: A lineage needs an anchor in space. The first generation is attached to a 'there', and later members call that place ancestral even if they have never lived there.
senses.whyCN: 谱系需要在空间里有一个锚点。第一代人与某个“那里”绑定，后来的成员即使从未在那里生活，也会称那个地方为祖居。

senses.title: Of an earlier biological form
senses.definition: relating to an earlier species, population, or character from which later forms evolved
senses.definitionCN: 与后来形态由之演化而来的早期物种、种群或性状有关的
senses.example: The fossil shows the ancestral wing structure of modern birds.
senses.exampleCN: 这块化石显示了现代鸟类祖先的翅膀结构。
senses.why: The family-tree image transfers from people to species: the form lower on the branch is the ancestor of the forms above it, so its traits are ancestral.
senses.whyCN: 家族树的意象从人转移到物种：分支下方的形态是上方形态的祖先，因此它的性状就是“祖先的”。

senses.title: Of rites and objects for the dead
senses.titleCN: 祭祀先人的：仪式与器物的
senses.definition: belonging to the ceremonies and objects used to honor dead forebears
senses.definitionCN: 属于纪念已故先人的仪式和器物的
senses.example: Incense smoke rose from the ancestral tablets in the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 祠堂里，祖先牌位前升起袅袅香烟。
senses.why: Honoring the dead gives the abstract link a concrete occasion. The tablet, hall, and rite are all 'of the ancestors' because they exist to address them.
senses.whyCN: 对死者的纪念给抽象的联系一个具体场合。牌位、祠堂和仪式都“属于祖先”，因为它们的存在就是为了向先人致意。

senses.title: Established by inherited custom
senses.definition: long established by inherited practice rather than by present choice
senses.definitionCN: 长期由继承下来的做法确立，而非由当下的选择确立
senses.example: The village still settles grazing disputes by ancestral custom.
senses.exampleCN: 这个村子仍按祖传习俗解决放牧纠纷。
senses.why: Custom can be inherited like land. If a rule is followed because the fathers followed it, it carries ancestral authority rather than merely being old.
senses.whyCN: 习俗可以像土地一样被继承。若一条规则因为父辈遵守而被遵守，它就带有祖制的权威，而不只是“古老”。

senses.title: An earlier model of a later thing
senses.definition: being an earlier model or version from which a later thing is metaphorically descended
senses.definitionCN: 作为后来事物在比喻意义上所由来的早期模型或版本
senses.example: The mechanical calculator is an ancestral device of the computer.
senses.exampleCN: 机械计算器是计算机的祖先式装置。
senses.why: Once 'descent' is used for anything that develops from something else, machines and institutions can have ancestors too; ancestral then means 'earlier in the line'.
senses.whyCN: 一旦“传承”被用于任何由他物发展而来的事物，机器和制度也可以有祖先；ancestral 于是表示“在谱系中更早的”。

senses.title: Of a people's shared origin
senses.definition: relating to the shared origin of a nation, tribe, or ethnic group
senses.definitionCN: 与民族、部落或族群共同来源有关的
senses.example: The exhibition maps the ancestral territory of the coastal tribes.
senses.exampleCN: 展览标出了沿海各部落的祖居地域。
senses.why: Ancestry can be imagined collectively: a whole people shares one set of forebears, so a land or language can be called ancestral for the group, not just for a family.
senses.whyCN: 血统可以被集体地想象：整个民族共享一批先人，因此一片土地或一种语言可以对群体而言是“祖辈的”，而不只对一个家庭而言。

senses.title: The reconstructed root of a language family
senses.titleCN: 语系中重构的原始形式
senses.definition: naming the oldest attested or reconstructed form from which a family of languages descends
senses.definitionCN: 指一个语系所由来的最古老的有证或重构形式
senses.example: The ancestral form of the word is marked with an asterisk in the dictionary.
senses.exampleCN: 这个词的原始形式在词典里用星号标出。
senses.why: Linguistic family trees put a reconstructed root at the base; because later languages 'descend' from it, the root is called ancestral even though no speaker ever used it.
senses.whyCN: 语言谱系树把重构的词根放在底部；因为后来的语言从它“传承”而来，这个词根就被称为原始形式，尽管从未有人真的使用过它。

intro.en: Ancestral is an adjective formed in English from ancestor, not an inherited Latin adjective. Its root is literal: ante- 'before' + cedere 'to go', so an ancestor is 'one who goes before'. Two common notes need correcting: ancient is not from antiquus but from ante via Vulgar Latin *anteanus; and descendant is not a cedere word (it is de- + scandere 'climb'). The opposite-direction cedere relative is successor.
intro.cn: ancestral 是英语在 ancestor 之后构成的形容词，不是直接继承的拉丁形容词。它的词根很字面：ante-“在前”+ cedere“走”，所以 ancestor 就是“走在前面的人”。两个常见说法需要纠正：ancient 并非来自 antiquus，而是经俗拉丁语 *anteanus 来自 ante；descendant 也不是 cedere 词（它是 de- + scandere“爬”）。真正与 cedere 反向对应的是 successor。

items.en: First recorded as 'pertaining to ancestors'. It was borrowed from Old French ancestrel (Anglo-French auncestrel), itself from ancestre 'ancestor'.
items.cn: 最早记录为“与祖先有关的”。它借自法语 ancestrel（盎格鲁法语 auncestrel），后者又来自 ancestre“祖先”。

items.en: Old French ancestre / ancessor (12c.) meant 'ancestor, forebear, forefather'. The English noun ancestor is recorded from c.1300 and took its current form in the early 15c.
items.cn: 古法语 ancestre / ancessor（12 世纪）意为“祖先、先人、父辈”。英语名词 ancestor 约在 1300 年有记录，15 世纪早期形成现在的拼写。

items.en: Ancestre goes back to Late Latin antecessor 'predecessor', literally 'fore-goer', an agent noun from the past-participle stem of antecedere 'to precede'.
items.cn: ancestre 可追溯到晚期拉丁语 antecessor“前任”，字面义为“先行者”，是 antecedere“走在前面”过去分词词干构成的施动名词。

items.en: antecedere = ante 'before' + cedere 'to go, yield'. The same cedere underlies predecessor and successor; successor (sub- 'after, near' + cedere) is the true opposite-direction relative, while descendant is not.
items.cn: antecedere = ante“在前”+ cedere“走、让步”。同一 cedere 也构成 predecessor 与 successor；successor（sub-“在后、靠近”+ cedere）才是真正反向对应的同根词，而 descendant 不是。

items.en: ante is traced to PIE *ant- 'front, forehead'; cedere to PIE *ked- 'to go, yield'. The reconstructions are standard, but the exact path through the Late Latin forms is not certain.
items.cn: ante 被追溯到原始印欧语 *ant-“前面、额头”；cedere 追溯到 *ked-“走、让步”。这些重构是通行的，但经过晚期拉丁语形式的具体路径并不完全确定。

items.en: The suffix -al (Latin -alis, through French) turns the noun into an adjective. Ancestorial (1650s) is an alternative. Note that ancient comes from ante + -anus, not from antiquus, and that ancestor and ancient share only the *ant- 'before' root, not the cedere part.
items.cn: 后缀 -al（拉丁 -alis，经法语）把名词变成形容词。ancestorial（17 世纪 50 年代）是替代形式。注意 ancient 来自 ante + -anus，而不是 antiquus；ancestor 与 ancient 只共享 *ant-“前”这个词根，并不共享 cedere 部分。

note.en: The first group separates true derivatives and look-alike forms from ancestral itself; the second compares words that are close in meaning but not interchangeable.
note.cn: 第一组把真正的派生形式与形近形式同 ancestral 本身分开；第二组比较意思接近但不能互换的词。

entries.definition: the person from whom one is descended; the noun that ancestral is formed from. It names a person, while ancestral describes what points back to that person.
entries.definitionCN: 某人所出自的先人；ancestral 由之构成的名词。它指一个人，而 ancestral 描述指向那个人的事物。

entries.definition: the whole line of descent, not one person. It is a collective noun and cannot replace ancestor in a sentence about a single forebear.
entries.definitionCN: 整条血统世系，而不是某一个人。它是集合名词，在指单个先人的句子里不能替代 ancestor。

entries.definition: very old or belonging to the distant past. It comes from Latin ante 'before' through Vulgar Latin *anteanus; it is not a derivative of ancestor, and its source is not antiquus (that is antique).
entries.definitionCN: 很古老的；属于遥远过去的。它经俗拉丁语 *anteanus 来自拉丁语 ante“前”；它不是 ancestor 的派生词，来源也不是 antiquus（后者给出 antique）。

entries.definition: a female ancestor. The -ess suffix marks feminine gender, not a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 女祖先。-ess 后缀只标记女性，不表示不同词根。

entries.definition: passing from parents to children through genes or legal inheritance. It stresses transmission, while ancestral stresses the people at the other end of the line.
entries.definitionCN: 通过基因或法定继承从父母传给子女。它强调传递过程，而 ancestral 强调这条线另一端的先人。

entries.definition: relating to a family as a social unit, especially shared traits or disease. It need not reach back generations, unlike ancestral.
entries.definitionCN: 与作为社会单位的家庭有关，尤指共享的特征或疾病。它不必追溯到许多代之前，这一点与 ancestral 不同。

entries.definition: received from a predecessor, especially a quality or condition. It is the result word; ancestral names the source relation.
entries.definitionCN: 从前人那里接收来的，尤指某种品质或状况。它是结果词，而 ancestral 命名的是来源关系。

entries.definition: existing from the very beginning of the world or of a species. It is much stronger and more remote than ancestral.
entries.definitionCN: 自世界或物种之初就存在的。它比 ancestral 强烈得多，也遥远得多。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: ancestor is ante- 'before' + cedere 'to go', the suffix -al makes the relation adjective, and the cedere family supplies the opposite-direction successor.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与真实同族词：ancestor 是 ante-“前”+ cedere“走”，后缀 -al 构成关系形容词，cedere 词族则提供反向的 successor。

normal.en: ancestor is ante- 'before' + cedere 'to go': the one who goes before.
normal.cn: ancestor 是 ante-“在前”+ cedere“走”：走在前面的人。

normal.en: -al means 'pertaining to', so ancestral simply means 'of the one who went before'.
normal.cn: -al 意为“与……有关的”，所以 ancestral 就是“属于走在前面那个人的”。

normal.en: Ancestor and ancient both start with ante 'before', but ancient is not a form of ancestor; antique is the word from antiquus.
normal.cn: ancestor 与 ancient 都以 ante“前”为源，但 ancient 不是 ancestor 的形式；来自 antiquus 的是 antique。

normal.en: Successor, from sub- + cedere, is the cedere relative meaning 'one who comes after'; descendant is from scandere 'to climb', not cedere.
normal.cn: successor 由 sub- + cedere 构成，是表示“后来者”的 cedere 同根词；descendant 来自 scandere“爬”，不是 cedere。

normal.en: Ancestral home, ancestral land and ancestral rites are fixed phrases for three branches: place, property, and ritual.
normal.cn: ancestral home、ancestral land、ancestral rites 是三条分支的固定搭配：地点、财产与仪式。

abstract.en: Picture a relay race in which every runner hands a baton forward; the runner behind you is ancestral, and the baton is what was inherited.
abstract.cn: 想象一场接力赛，每个跑者把接力棒向前交；你身后的那位跑者是“祖先”，接力棒就是被继承下来的东西。

abstract.en: A family tree drawn on paper: every line above your name is an ancestor, and the whole upper part of the tree is your ancestry.
abstract.cn: 纸上画的一棵家谱树：你名字上方的每一条线都是 ancestor，整棵树上方的部分就是你的 ancestry。

abstract.en: The same tree can hold species or languages: the root is the ancestral form, and every branch above it descends from that root.
abstract.cn: 同一棵树也能容纳物种或语言：根是 ancestral form，上方每一根枝条都从那个根传承而来。

examples.en: Her ancestral home stands at the end of the lane.
examples.cn: 她的祖宅立在巷子尽头。

examples.en: The researchers compared the ancestral species with its modern relatives.
examples.cn: 研究人员把那个祖先物种与现代近亲作了比较。

examples.en: The festival includes ancestral rites that date back centuries.
examples.cn: 这个节庆包含可追溯数百年的祭祖仪式。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安祖传」——‘安’家的东西祖上传下来 → ancestral 祖传的、祖先的（只借音，不表词源）

root: 源自拉丁语 antecessor“先行者”，由 ante“在前”+ cedere“走”构成，核心是“走在前面的人”；-al 使其成为形容词。

sensesIntro.en: Nine uses of ancestral all point backwards along a line: a person, a possession, a homeland, a species, a rite, a custom, a machine, a people, or a language can all have something standing earlier behind it.
sensesIntro.cn: ancestral 的九个用法都沿着一条线向后指：一个人、一份财产、一片故乡、一个物种、一种仪式、一种习俗、一台机器、一个民族或一种语言，背后都可以站着更早的东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: everything that points back along a line to the ones who went before.
core.cn: 核心意象：一切沿着一条线指向“走在前面的人”的事物。

branches.en: PERSONS AND PROPERTY: the relation to a forebear, and what that forebear handed down.
branches.cn: 人与财产：与先人的关系，以及先人传下的东西。

branches.en: PLACES AND PEOPLES: a homeland anchors a family, and a shared homeland anchors a whole people.
branches.cn: 地点与族群：故乡为家族提供锚点，共同的故土为一个民族提供锚点。

branches.en: BIOLOGY AND LANGUAGE: species and language families are drawn as trees, with an ancestral form at the base.
branches.cn: 生物与语言：物种和语系都被画成树，底部是 ancestral form。

branches.en: RITUAL AND CUSTOM: the dead are addressed through rites, and their practice becomes inherited authority.
branches.cn: 仪式与习俗：人们通过仪式向死者致意，而这些做法又成为继承下来的权威。

branches.en: METAPHORICAL LINEAGE: machines and institutions can have earlier models, so the family-tree image extends beyond blood.
branches.cn: 比喻谱系：机器和制度也可以有早期模型，家族树意象因此超出血缘。

intro.en: Ancestral is a living English adjective built from ancestor + -al. The base noun is a French and Latin loan whose parts are frozen: ante- 'before' + cedere 'to go'. English adds -al, -ess, -ly and -ial to the finished family, while the same Latin root also arrives in predecessor, successor and antecedent.
intro.cn: ancestral 是由 ancestor + -al 构成的活的英语形容词。基础名词是法语和拉丁语借词，内部成分已经凝固：ante-“前”+ cedere“走”。英语在成品词族上加 -al、-ess、-ly、-ial，而同一拉丁词根也通过 predecessor、successor、antecedent 进入英语。

latinIntro.en: The Latin source is antecedere 'to precede' and its agent noun antecessor 'fore-goer'. Cedere 'to go, yield' also gives predecessor and successor. Descendant belongs to scandere 'to climb', so it is a look-alike rather than a cedere relative.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语来源是 antecedere“走在前面”及其施动名词 antecessor“先行者”。cedere“走、让步”也构成 predecessor 与 successor。descendant 属于 scandere“爬”，因此是形近词，而不是 cedere 的同根词。

items.meaningCN: 祖先的；与先人有关的（-al 构成关系形容词）
items.example: The ancestral portrait was cleaned before the reunion.
items.exampleCN: 聚会前，那幅先人画像被清理干净。

items.structure: Latin ante- (before) + cedere (go), through Late Latin antecessor
items.meaning: one who goes before; a forebear
items.meaningCN: 走在前面的人；祖先（ante- 前 + cedere 走）
items.example: Her earliest known ancestor arrived by boat in 1840.
items.exampleCN: 她已知最早的那位祖先于 1840 年乘船抵达。

items.meaningCN: 血统；世系（-ry 构成集合名词）
items.example: The archive traces the family's ancestry to three counties.
items.exampleCN: 档案把这个家族的血统追溯到三个县。

items.example: The ancestress is remembered for founding the village school.
items.exampleCN: 这位女祖先因创办村校而被铭记。

items.meaning: in a way that relates to ancestors
items.meaningCN: 在祖先方面；按祖先的方式（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The land was ancestrally held by the same clan.
items.exampleCN: 这片土地在祖先意义上由同一宗族持有。

items.meaning: relating to ancestors; a variant of ancestral
items.meaningCN: 祖先的（ancestral 的替代形容词形式）
items.example: The older texts prefer ancestorial rights to ancestral rights.
items.exampleCN: 较早的文本更常用 ancestorial rights，而不是 ancestral rights。

items.meaning: a thing or person that comes before
items.meaningCN: 前事；先行者（ante- 前 + cedere 走 + -ent）
items.example: The antecedent of the modern treaty was a verbal promise.
items.exampleCN: 现代条约的前身是一句口头承诺。

items.meaning: someone or something that came before another in an office or line
items.meaningCN: 前任；前身（prae- 前 + de- 离 + cedere 走）
items.example: The predecessor of the current director served for twenty years.
items.exampleCN: 现任主管的前任任职二十年。

items.meaningCN: 继任者；后继者（sub- 后 + cedere 走）
items.example: The successor took office in the following spring.
items.exampleCN: 继任者在次年春天上任。

items.structure: de- (down) + scandere (climb); not a cedere word
items.meaning: a person or thing that comes from an earlier one
items.meaningCN: 后代；衍生物（de- 下 + scandere 爬；注意它不是 cedere 的同根词）
items.example: The descendant of that tree still stands in the courtyard.
items.exampleCN: 那棵树的后代仍立在院子里。

items.structure: Latin ante (before) + -anus, through Vulgar Latin *anteanus; not from antiquus
items.meaningCN: 古老的；古代的（ante 前 + -anus；并非来自 antiquus）
items.example: The ancient wall follows the old city boundary.
items.exampleCN: 那道古墙沿着旧城边界延伸。

latinEntries.structure: Latin verb; source of descend and descendant, not of ancestor
latinEntries.meaningCN: 爬；攀登（descend/descendant 的来源，不是 ancestor 的来源）

definition_zh: n. 舰队（尤指一五八八年西班牙无敌舰队）；一大群同向行进的车船飞机
definition_en: A large fleet of warships, especially the Spanish fleet sent against England; by extension, any large group of vehicles moving together.
core_image: 一整片船帆压过来，数都数不清
scene: 西班牙派出无敌舰队远征英格兰。 Spain sent the Armada against England.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：armada 指大批战舰组成的舰队，大写 the Armada 特指西班牙无敌舰队。

pos.zh: 舰队；一大群行进的车船

senses.title: A great fleet of warships
senses.definition: a large group of armed ships sailing together, the sense made famous by the Spanish fleet
senses.definitionCN: 一同航行的大批武装船只，因西班牙舰队而闻名
senses.example: The armada stretched along the horizon.
senses.exampleCN: 舰队沿着地平线铺开。
senses.why: The word is built on arms, weapons, so an armada is literally an armed mass, a crowd defined by its weapons.
senses.whyCN: 这个词建在 arms「武器」之上，所以 armada 字面就是「武装起来的一大群」，由武器定义的群体。

senses.title: Any mass moving together
senses.titleCN: 任何一同移动的庞大群体
senses.definition: by extension, a large number of vehicles, boats or aircraft travelling as one body
senses.definitionCN: 引申指作为一个整体行进的大量车辆、船只或飞机
senses.example: An armada of delivery vans filled the narrow lane.
senses.exampleCN: 一大群送货车挤满了那条窄巷。
senses.why: Once the naval picture was fixed, the striking part was the sheer number, so the word spread to any impressive procession.
senses.whyCN: 海军画面固定之后，最醒目的是数量之多，于是这个词扩展到任何气势庞大的行列。

intro.en: Armada is Spanish armada, fleet, from armado, armed, from Latin armata, an armed force, the participle of armare, to arm, from arma, weapons.
intro.cn: armada 就是西班牙语 armada「舰队」，来自 armado「武装的」，而后者出自拉丁语 armata「武装力量」，是 armare「武装」的分词，词根为 arma「武器」。

items.en: Latin arma meant arms or weapons, and also the fittings of a ship, which links weapons and sailing early on.
items.cn: 拉丁语 arma 意为「武器」，也指船上的装备，很早就把武器与航海连在一起。

items.en: The verb armare meant to furnish with weapons, to equip a man or a vessel for fighting.
items.cn: 动词 armare 意为「配备武器」，即为人员或船只装上作战装备。

items.en: Its feminine participle armata came to mean an armed force, the ancestor of army and armada alike.
items.cn: 其阴性分词 armata 转而指「武装力量」，是 army 与 armada 共同的祖先。

items.en: Spanish armada named a fleet, keeping the naval side of arma that other languages dropped.
items.cn: 西班牙语 armada 指舰队，保留了 arma 中其他语言丢掉的航海一面。

items.en: English borrowed armada in the 1530s as a general word for a large fleet of warships.
items.cn: 英语在 1530 年代借入 armada，泛指大批战舰组成的舰队。

items.en: The failed Spanish invasion of 1588 froze the capitalised Armada into English memory as one specific fleet.
items.cn: 1588 年西班牙入侵失败，使大写的 Armada 在英语记忆中定格为那支特定舰队。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the arms family together and adds armadillo, Spanish for the little armed one; the near-meaning group lists words for groups of ships.
note.cn: 形近组把「武器」词族排在一起，并加上 armadillo——西班牙语「披甲的小家伙」；近义组列出表示船群的词。

entries.definition: A large body of soldiers.
Weapons and military equipment.
Protective covering for the body.
A mammal with a bony shell.
A group of ships under one command.
A small fleet of little vessels.
entries.definitionCN: 小型船只组成的小舰队。

entries.definition: A formed unit of ships or aircraft.
entries.definitionCN: 舰艇或飞机的编队单位。

entries.definition: Ships travelling together for protection.
entries.definitionCN: 为互相护卫而同行的船队。

normalIntro.en: Armada is arm plus the Spanish group ending -ada: an armed mass, which at sea means a fleet.
normalIntro.cn: armada 就是 arm 加西班牙语群体后缀 -ada：武装起来的一大群，在海上就是舰队。

normal.en: Capitalised Armada means the Spanish fleet of 1588.
normal.cn: 大写的 Armada 指 1588 年西班牙舰队。

normal.en: Lower case armada can describe vans or planes.
normal.cn: 小写 armada 可形容送货车或机群。

normal.en: The pattern is an armada of plus a plural noun.
normal.cn: 常见句式是 an armada of 加复数名词。

normal.en: Army is land, armada is sea, both from arma.
normal.cn: army 在陆，armada 在海，都出自 arma。

normal.en: Armadillo is the same Spanish root, little armed one.
normal.cn: armadillo 同源，意为「披甲的小家伙」。

abstract.en: Picture sails filling the whole horizon.
abstract.cn: 想象船帆填满整条地平线。

abstract.en: Imagine a lane packed end to end with vans.
abstract.cn: 想象一条巷子首尾挤满送货车。

abstract.en: Think of a crowd whose size is the message.
abstract.cn: 想象一群以数量本身说话的东西。

examples.en: An armada of fishing boats left at dawn.
examples.cn: 一大群渔船在黎明出发。

examples.en: The two armadas met off the headland.
examples.cn: 两支舰队在海岬外相遇。

examples.en: He arrived with an armada of removal vans.
examples.cn: 他带着一大群搬家货车抵达。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：arm「武器」+ -ada「一大群」——武装起来的一整群船，就是舰队 armada。

root: 拉丁语 arma「武器、船具」生出 armare「武装」，分词 armata「武装力量」在西班牙语中作 armada「舰队」；1588 年西班牙入侵使大写 Armada 专指那支舰队。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are one armed mass: warships sailing as a body, and any procession whose sheer number makes the same impression.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项是同一群「武装的庞大群体」：作为一个整体航行的战舰，以及任何以数量造成同样印象的行列。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a whole spread of sails bearing down, too many to count
core.cn: 核心意象：一整片船帆压过来，数都数不清

branches.en: Sails filling the horizon.
branches.cn: 填满地平线的船帆。

branches.en: Two fleets meeting off a headland.
branches.cn: 在海岬外相遇的两支舰队。

branches.en: A lane packed with delivery vans.
branches.cn: 挤满送货车的窄巷。

branches.en: Fishing boats leaving as one body.
branches.cn: 作为一个整体出海的渔船群。

branches.en: Both impress by number alone.
branches.cn: 两者都仅凭数量就令人震动。

intro.en: Armada is arm plus the Spanish collective ending -ada; the same root builds army, armour, armament and disarm.
intro.cn: armada 是 arm 加西班牙语集合后缀 -ada；同一词根还构成 army、armour、armament 与 disarm。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is arma, weapons, armare, to arm, and armata, an armed force; navis, ship, gives navy beside it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语层次是 arma「武器」、armare「武装」与 armata「武装力量」；旁边的 navis「船」产生 navy。

latinEntries.exampleCN: arma 是整个词族的起点。
armare 产生 arm 与 armour。
armata 给出西班牙语 armada。

definition_zh: n. 避免；回避；躲开；（法律上）宣告无效；撤销
definition_en: The act of keeping away from or preventing something; in law, the making of a document void.
core_image: 提前绕开那个坑的那一步
scene: 他把回避冲突当成习惯，结果问题越积越多。 He made avoidance of conflict a habit, and the problems piled up.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：avoidance 指有意躲开或防止某事发生这一行为。

pos.zh: 避免；回避；（法律）撤销

senses.title: Keeping away from
senses.definition: the practice of staying clear of a person, subject or situation
senses.definitionCN: 有意远离某人、某话题或某处境的做法
senses.example: His avoidance of eye contact was obvious.
senses.exampleCN: 他明显在回避目光接触。
senses.why: Avoid came from a French phrase meaning to make empty, so avoidance is the act of clearing something out of your path.
senses.whyCN: avoid 源自意为「清空」的法语短语，因此 avoidance 就是把某物从自己路径上清开的行为。

senses.title: Preventing an outcome
senses.definition: the deliberate prevention of an unwanted event, as in arranging affairs so a burden never falls due
senses.definitionCN: 有意防止不良事件发生，例如事先安排事务使某项负担不落到头上
senses.example: Tax avoidance is legal, unlike evasion.
senses.exampleCN: 避税合法，与逃税不同。
senses.why: The same clearing idea applies before the event, so the word covers arranging affairs in advance.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「清空」思路用在事件之前，于是这个词也涵盖事先安排事务。

senses.title: Making void in law
senses.definition: in legal use, the act of making a contract or instrument void
senses.definitionCN: 在法律用法中，指使合同或文书无效的行为
senses.example: The clause provided for avoidance of the policy.
senses.exampleCN: 该条款规定了保单的撤销。
senses.why: This sense keeps the original empty meaning literally: the document is emptied of legal force.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项字面保留了「空」的本义：文书的法律效力被清空。

intro.en: Avoidance is avoid plus -ance; avoid comes from Anglo-French avoider, to clear out, from es-, out, and vuide, empty, related to Latin vacuus.
intro.cn: avoidance 是 avoid 加 -ance；avoid 来自盎格鲁法语 avoider「清空」，由 es-「向外」与 vuide「空」构成，与拉丁语 vacuus 相关。

items.en: Latin vacuus meant empty, the source of vacant and vacuum.
items.cn: 拉丁语 vacuus 意为「空的」，是 vacant 与 vacuum 的来源。

items.en: Old French vuide meant empty, and vuidier meant to empty out.
items.cn: 古法语 vuide 意为「空」，vuidier 意为「腾空」。

items.en: With es-, out, prefixed, avoider meant to clear out or withdraw.
items.cn: 加上 es-「向外」构成 avoider，意为「清空、撤出」。

items.en: Middle English avoiden meant to remove, expel or leave empty.
items.cn: 中古英语 avoiden 意为「移走、驱逐、腾空」。

items.en: The noun is recorded early, kept in law for making a document void.
items.cn: 该名词出现很早，在法律中保留「使文书无效」之义。

items.en: By the fifteenth century the verb had settled into keeping clear of something.
items.cn: 到十五世纪动词已定型为「躲开某事物」。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the void family; the near-meaning group lists other words for staying clear of something.
note.cn: 形近组保留 void 词族；近义组列出其他表示远离某事物的词。

entries.definition: To keep clear of something.
Able to be prevented.
Empty, or of no legal force.
A very large quantity.
Dodging a duty by trickery.
Stopping something before it happens.
Deliberately keeping away from.
The act of pulling back.

normalIntro.en: Avoidance is avoid plus -ance: the act of emptying your path of something you do not want.
normalIntro.cn: avoidance 是 avoid 加 -ance：把不想要的东西从自己路径上清开的行为。

normal.en: Tax avoidance is legal; tax evasion is not.
normal.cn: tax avoidance 合法，tax evasion 不合法。

normal.en: The pattern is avoidance of plus a noun.
normal.cn: 常见句式是 avoidance of 加名词。

normal.en: Avoidance behaviour is a psychology term.
normal.cn: avoidance behaviour 是心理学术语。

normal.en: The adjective pair is avoidable and unavoidable.
normal.cn: 形容词一对是 avoidable 与 unavoidable。

normal.en: A set clause opens with a phrase about doubt.
normal.cn: 有个固定条款以「为免生疑义」开头。

abstract.en: Picture a step sideways around a hole.
abstract.cn: 想象绕开坑洞的侧向一步。

abstract.en: Imagine a gaze that never lands on yours.
abstract.cn: 想象一道从不落到你身上的目光。

abstract.en: Think of a contract drained of its force.
abstract.cn: 想象一份被抽走效力的合同。

examples.en: Avoidance of delay saved the contract.
examples.cn: 避免延误保住了这份合同。

examples.en: Fear often shows itself as avoidance.
examples.cn: 恐惧常表现为回避。

examples.en: The policy allows avoidance for fraud.
examples.cn: 该保单允许因欺诈而撤销。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：avoid「躲开、清空」+ -ance「行为」——把不想要的东西从路上清开，这一行为就是 avoidance。

root: 拉丁语 vacuus「空」经古法语 vuide 加 es-「向外」成 avoider「清空」，入中古英语作 avoiden「躲开」；加 -ance 成 avoidance，法律中保留「使无效」的本义。

sensesIntro.en: All three senses empty something out of the way: a person or topic, an unwanted outcome, or the legal force of a document.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项都在把某物清开：某人或某话题、不想要的结果，或文书的法律效力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the step taken early to go around the hole
core.cn: 核心意象：提前绕开那个坑的那一步

branches.en: A gaze kept off the other person.
branches.cn: 不落在对方身上的目光。

branches.en: Conflict pushed out of the way.
branches.cn: 被推开的冲突。

branches.en: Affairs arranged so no tax falls due.
branches.cn: 安排得不产生税负的事务。

branches.en: A policy emptied of legal force.
branches.cn: 被抽走法律效力的保单。

branches.en: Both clear the path before trouble.
branches.cn: 两者都在麻烦之前清出路径。

intro.en: Avoidance is avoid plus -ance; avoid hides es-, out, and vuide, empty, which also give void and vacuum.
intro.cn: avoidance 是 avoid 加 -ance；avoid 里藏着 es-「向外」与 vuide「空」，它们也产生 void 与 vacuum。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is vacuus, empty, and vacare, to be empty; the -ance ending is Latin -antia.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语层次是 vacuus「空」与 vacare「空着」；-ance 词尾即拉丁语 -antia。

definition_zh: n. 女低音；女低音歌手；中音乐器（如中音萨克斯）
definition_en: The lowest adult female singing voice, a singer who takes that line, or an instrument whose range matches it, such as an alto saxophone.
core_image: 合唱里托在主旋律下方的那一层声音
scene: 合唱团缺了中间那一层，排练时和声总是空着。 The choir needs one more alto before Friday.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：合唱团里唱女低音声部的那个人。指挥说周五之前还要再招一位，否则中间那层和声一直空着。

pos.zh: 女低音；女低音歌手；中音乐器

senses.title: The low female line
senses.titleCN: 女低音声部；女低音歌手
senses.definition: the lowest adult female singing voice, or a singer who performs that part in a choir
senses.definitionCN: 成年女性最低的歌唱声部，或在合唱团中演唱该声部的歌手
senses.example: She moved from soprano to alto after her voice settled.
senses.exampleCN: 嗓音定型后，她从女高音转到女低音。
senses.why: Italian alto meant high, because the line was once the high part sung by men above the tenor; when women took it over, the same name came to mean the lowest female line.
senses.whyCN: 意大利语 alto 意为「高」，因为这条旋律线曾是男声在男高音之上唱的高声部；女性接手后，同一个名称就转而指最低的女声线。

senses.title: An instrument of that range
senses.definition: an instrument built to cover the same range as that voice, as in an alto saxophone or alto flute
senses.definitionCN: 音域与该人声声部相当的乐器，如中音萨克斯或中音长笛
senses.example: He bought a second-hand alto for the school band.
senses.exampleCN: 他为学校乐队买了一把二手中音萨克斯。
senses.why: Instruments are labelled by the voice range they replace, so alto travels from the choir stall to the brass shelf without changing its meaning.
senses.whyCN: 乐器按其替代的人声音域标注，因此 alto 从合唱席位走到铜管乐器架上，含义并未改变。

intro.en: Alto is Italian for high, from Latin altus, which in turn comes from alere, to nourish. The name stayed the same while the range it described moved from a high male part to the lowest female one.
intro.cn: alto 是意大利语的「高」，来自拉丁语 altus，而 altus 又来自 alere「滋养」。名称一直没变，它所描述的音域却从男声的高声部移到了最低的女声部。

items.en: Latin altus meant high or tall, and originally grown or nourished, from the verb alere, to feed and bring up. Height was pictured as the result of being fed.
items.cn: 拉丁语 altus 意为「高的、高的」，最初指「长成的、被养育的」，来自动词 alere「喂养、养育」。高度被想象为被喂养的结果。

items.en: Italian kept alto for high. In church music the alto line sat above the tenor and was sung by men, so the part was genuinely the high one.
items.cn: 意大利语保留 alto 表示「高」。在教堂音乐中，alto 声部位于男高音之上，由男声演唱，因此那确实是高声部。

items.en: English took alto in the eighteenth century as a musical term for that male high part, along with the Italian vocabulary of tempo and dynamics.
items.cn: 英语在 18 世纪把 alto 作为音乐术语借入，指那个男声高声部，同时借入的还有意大利语的速度与力度词汇。

items.en: When women replaced the male singers, the line sounded an octave lower in absolute terms, and alto came to name the lowest female voice. The label kept its old shape.
items.cn: 当女性取代男歌手后，这条线在绝对音高上低了一个八度，alto 于是转指最低的女声。标签保留了旧的样子。

items.en: Modern English uses alto for the voice, the singer and instruments of that range, while the same Latin altus survives in altitude and altimeter.
items.cn: 现代英语用 alto 指声部、歌手以及该音域的乐器，而同一个拉丁语 altus 仍保存在 altitude 与 altimeter 中。

note.en: The look-alike group separates alto from altar and alter, then keeps the alt- height family; the near-meaning group lists neighbouring voice ranges.
note.cn: 形近组先把 alto 与 altar、alter 分开，再保留 alt-「高」词族；近义组列出相邻的声部名称。

entries.definition: A table used in religious rites.
entries.definitionCN: 宗教仪式中使用的台子。

entries.definition: To change something slightly.
Height above sea level.
An instrument that shows height.
The lowest female voice, richer than a plain alto.
entries.definitionCN: 最低的女声，比一般女低音更厚。

entries.definition: A female voice between soprano and alto.
entries.definitionCN: 介于女高音与女低音之间的女声。

entries.definition: The high adult male singing voice.
A male voice singing in the alto range.

normalIntro.en: Alto is the Italian word for high, so link it to altitude and remember that the range moved, not the name.
normalIntro.cn: alto 就是意大利语的「高」，把它和 altitude 联系起来，记住变的是音域，不是名字。

normal.en: Altitude and alto share the same Latin altus, so height is the hook.
normal.cn: altitude 与 alto 共用拉丁语 altus，所以「高」就是记忆钩。

normal.en: The plural is altos, not alti: the word is treated as English now.
normal.cn: 复数是 altos，不是 alti：这个词现在按英语处理。

normal.en: Say alto saxophone as one chunk; nobody says alto sax in formal writing.
normal.cn: 把 alto saxophone 当一个整体记；正式书面语不说 alto sax。

normal.en: Do not confuse alto with altar, the church table, or alter, to change.
normal.cn: 别把 alto 与 altar「祭坛」或 alter「改变」混淆。

normal.en: In a four-part choir the order top down is soprano, alto, tenor, bass.
normal.cn: 四部合唱自上而下是女高音、女低音、男高音、男低音。

abstract.en: Picture a warm middle layer holding up a thin bright tune.
abstract.cn: 想象一层温暖的中音托着一条细亮的主旋律。

abstract.en: Imagine a brass instrument sitting between two larger ones on a shelf.
abstract.cn: 想象架子上两件大乐器之间夹着一件铜管乐器。

abstract.en: Think of a name that stayed still while the voice underneath it changed.
abstract.cn: 想象一个名字停在原处，而它底下的嗓音已经换了。

examples.en: The alto line carries most of the inner harmony.
examples.cn: 女低音声部承担了大部分内声部和声。

examples.en: She sings alto in the village choir.
examples.cn: 她在村里合唱团唱女低音。

examples.en: Two altos were absent, so the chord sounded thin.
examples.cn: 两位女低音缺席，和弦听起来很单薄。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「奥托」——奥（al）托（to）：在下面托住主旋律的那层声音，就是女低音；托得高一点的就是中音萨克斯。

root: 拉丁语 alere「滋养」生出 altus「高的」，意大利语沿用为 alto「高」，原指男声在男高音之上的高声部；女声接手后转指最低女声，并按音域引申到中音乐器。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are one range named twice: first the human line in a choir, then the instrument built to cover the same span.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项是同一个音域被命名两次：先是合唱团里的人声线，再是为覆盖同一跨度而造的乐器。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the warm layer holding up the tune from below
core.cn: 核心意象：从下方托住主旋律的那层温暖声音

branches.en: A singer taking the inner line.
branches.cn: 唱内声部的歌手。

branches.en: A choir short of its middle layer.
branches.cn: 缺少中间层的合唱团。

branches.en: A saxophone of middle range.
branches.cn: 中音域的萨克斯。

branches.en: A clef written for that range.
branches.cn: 为该音域书写的谱号。

branches.en: One range, named for voice and instrument.
branches.cn: 同一个音域，分别用于人声与乐器。

intro.en: Alto carries the Latin alt- height root, which also builds altitude, altimeter and exalt.
intro.cn: alto 带着拉丁语 alt-「高」词根，这个词根还构成 altitude、altimeter 与 exalt。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is altus, high, from alere, to nourish; Italian passed alto into English unchanged.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语层次是 altus「高的」，来自 alere「滋养」；意大利语把 alto 原样传入英语。

latinEntries.exampleCN: altus 产生意大利语 alto。
alere 是 altus 的来源。

definition_zh: n. 脊柱；脊椎；骨干；支柱；骨气；坚毅
definition_en: The spine; the main support or strongest part of a system; firmness of character.
core_image: 撑起整个身子的那一串骨头
scene: 她是整个项目的骨干，谁的活卡住都找她。 She was the backbone of the project, and everyone came to her when work stalled.
sceneCN: 第 2 个义项：backbone 比喻一个组织或系统中起支撑作用的核心部分。

pos.zh: 脊柱；骨干；骨气

senses.title: The row of back bones
senses.definition: the line of joined bones running down the back, which holds the body upright
senses.definitionCN: 沿背部相连的一列骨头，支撑身体直立
senses.example: He injured his backbone in the fall.
senses.exampleCN: 他在跌倒中伤到了脊柱。
senses.why: Backbone is back plus bone, naming the structure by where it sits and what it is made of.
senses.whyCN: backbone 由 back 与 bone 组成，用位置与材质来命名这个结构。

senses.title: The main support
senses.definition: the part of a system, group or network on which everything else depends
senses.definitionCN: 系统、群体或网络中其余部分都依赖的那一部分
senses.example: Small farms are the backbone of the region.
senses.exampleCN: 小农场是该地区的支柱。
senses.why: Because the spine holds the whole body, the word moved to whatever holds a whole organisation together.
senses.whyCN: 因为脊柱撑起整个身体，这个词便转指任何把整个组织撑起来的东西。

senses.title: Firmness of character
senses.definition: the courage to hold a position under pressure, thought of as an inner spine
senses.definitionCN: 在压力下坚持立场的勇气，被看作内在的脊梁
senses.example: It takes backbone to admit a mistake.
senses.exampleCN: 承认错误需要骨气。
senses.why: A body without a spine collapses, so a person without firmness was described as having no backbone.
senses.whyCN: 没有脊柱的身体会塌下去，因此没有坚定立场的人就被说成没有 backbone。

intro.en: Backbone is back plus bone, both native English words; the anatomical sense is medieval, and the figurative senses of support and courage follow from it.
intro.cn: backbone 是 back 加 bone，两者都是英语本族词；解剖义见于中世纪，「支柱」与「骨气」的比喻义由此衍生。

items.en: Old English baec meant the back of a body, the surface opposite the chest.
items.cn: 古英语 baec 意为「身体的背部」，即与胸相对的那一面。

items.en: Old English ban meant a bone, and also the hard inner part of anything.
items.cn: 古英语 ban 意为「骨」，也指任何事物的坚硬内核。

items.en: Middle English backbon named the spine as the bone of the back.
items.cn: 中古英语 backbon 用「背之骨」来指脊柱。

items.en: From the sixteenth century the word named the chief support of a structure or group.
items.cn: 自十六世纪起，这个词指某结构或群体的主要支撑。

items.en: In the nineteenth century it came to mean firmness of will, often in the negative.
items.cn: 十九世纪它转指意志的坚定，常用于否定表述。

items.en: Computing borrowed it for the main line that carries traffic between smaller networks.
items.cn: 计算机领域借它指在较小网络之间承载流量的主干线路。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the back compounds; the near-meaning group lists words for a spine, a support and a firm will.
note.cn: 形近组保留 back 复合词；近义组列出表示脊柱、支撑与坚定意志的词。

entries.definition: A dull pain in the back.
A stage cloth, or a setting.
A hard part of the skeleton.
Exhaustingly hard.
The column of back bones.
The chief thing relied on.
A supporting column or person.
Tough persistence of will.

normalIntro.en: Backbone is back plus bone: the spine that holds you up, then anything that holds a system or a will up.
normalIntro.cn: backbone 是 back 加 bone：撑起你的脊柱，进而指撑起某个系统或某种意志的东西。

normal.en: The backbone of something is the set phrase.
normal.cn: 固定说法是 the backbone of 某事物。

normal.en: Spine is the medical word, backbone the plain one.
normal.cn: spine 是医学用词，backbone 更平易。

normal.en: No backbone means no firmness.
normal.cn: 没有 backbone 就是没有骨气。

normal.en: Networks use it for the main line.
normal.cn: 网络领域用它指主干线路。

normal.en: The plural backbones is rare but regular.
normal.cn: 复数 backbones 少见但规则。

abstract.en: Picture a stack of blocks holding a body tall.
abstract.cn: 想象一摞骨块把身体撑高。

abstract.en: Imagine one beam carrying a whole roof.
abstract.cn: 想象一根梁撑起整个屋顶。

abstract.en: Think of a person who will not bend.
abstract.cn: 想象一个不肯弯下的人。

examples.en: The scan showed a healthy backbone.
examples.cn: 扫描显示脊柱健康。

examples.en: Rail is the backbone of freight here.
examples.cn: 铁路是这里货运的支柱。

examples.en: She showed real backbone in the meeting.
examples.cn: 她在会上表现出真正的骨气。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：back「背」+ bone「骨」——背上的那串骨头就是脊柱；撑起组织的是骨干，撑起人的是骨气。

root: 古英语 baec「背」与 ban「骨」合成中古英语 backbon「脊柱」；因脊柱撑起全身，十六世纪衍生「支柱」义，十九世纪再衍生「骨气」义。

sensesIntro.en: All three senses are the same holding-up: bones holding a body, a core holding a system, and will holding a person.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项都是同一种「撑起」：骨头撑起身体，核心撑起系统，意志撑起一个人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the string of bones that holds the whole body up
core.cn: 核心意象：撑起整个身子的那一串骨头

branches.en: A spine injured in a fall.
branches.cn: 跌倒中受伤的脊柱。

branches.en: A scan showing healthy bones.
branches.cn: 显示骨骼健康的扫描。

branches.en: A person the whole project leans on.
branches.cn: 整个项目依赖的人。

branches.en: Rail carrying the freight of a region.
branches.cn: 承载一地货运的铁路。

branches.en: A will that refuses to bend.
branches.cn: 不肯弯曲的意志。

intro.en: Backbone is back plus bone; the same back element builds backdrop and backpack, while -y turns bone into bony.
intro.cn: backbone 是 back 加 bone；同一 back 成分构成 backdrop 与 backpack，而 -y 把 bone 变成 bony。

latinIntro.en: Both halves are native; Latin spina, thorn, gives spine and spinal, and Latin columna gives column and pillar beside them.
latinIntro.cn: 两个部分都属本族语；拉丁语 spina「刺」产生 spine 与 spinal，columna 则产生 column，旁边还有 pillar。

definition_zh: n. 热情，激情，热切（英式拼作 ardour）；（旧用）灼热，炽热
definition_en: Intense enthusiasm or passion for a person, cause or activity; in older use, burning heat. British English spells it ardour.
core_image: 胸口那团一直烧着的火
scene: 他把全部热情投进了这项研究。 He threw all his ardor into the research.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：ardor 指对人、事业或活动强烈的热情，英式拼写为 ardour。

pos.zh: 热情；激情；热切；灼热

senses.title: Burning enthusiasm
senses.definition: strong, eager feeling for a person, belief or work, the sense almost always intended today
senses.definitionCN: 对某人、某信念或某项工作强烈而急切的感情，是今天几乎唯一使用的义项
senses.example: She defended the plan with unexpected ardor.
senses.exampleCN: 她以出人意料的热情为该计划辩护。
senses.why: The Latin root means burn, so ardor is feeling described as fire: it warms, it spreads and it can go out.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根意为「烧」，所以 ardor 是把感情当火来写：它会发热、会蔓延，也会熄灭。

senses.title: Physical burning heat
senses.definition: in older or poetic use, intense heat itself, the literal sense the figurative one grew from
senses.definitionCN: 在较旧或诗歌用法中指强烈的热本身，是比喻义所由来的字面义
senses.example: The poem speaks of the ardor of the noon sun.
senses.exampleCN: 诗中写到正午太阳的灼热。
senses.why: This is the older layer: before ardor meant eagerness it meant temperature, which is why ardent still describes both.
senses.whyCN: 这是较古的一层：ardor 在指热切之前先指温度，所以 ardent 至今两者都能形容。

intro.en: Ardor is Latin ardor, flame or eagerness, from ardere, to burn. English took it through Old French ardour, and American spelling later dropped the u.
intro.cn: ardor 就是拉丁语 ardor「火焰、热切」，来自 ardere「燃烧」。英语经古法语 ardour 吸收，美式拼写后来去掉了 u。

items.en: The reconstructed root as- meant to burn or glow, and it also lies behind ash and arid.
items.cn: 重构词根 as- 意为「燃烧、发光」，它也是 ash 与 arid 的来源。

items.en: Latin ardere meant to be on fire, and its participle ardens gave English ardent.
items.cn: 拉丁语 ardere 意为「着火」，其分词 ardens 给出英语 ardent。

items.en: The noun ardor named a flame, then heat, then the heat of feeling, all in one word.
items.cn: 名词 ardor 先指火焰，再指热，再指感情的热度，都在同一个词里。

items.en: Old French ardour carried the word north with the u that British spelling still keeps.
items.cn: 古法语 ardour 带着那个 u 北上，英式拼写至今保留。

items.en: English recorded the word in the fourteenth century for both burning heat and eager passion.
items.cn: 英语在 14 世纪记录该词，兼指灼热与热切的激情。

items.en: American reform dropped the u to give ardor, while British usage kept ardour; both are correct.
items.cn: 美式改革去掉 u 成 ardor，英式保留 ardour，两者都对。

note.en: The look-alike group warns against order and odor, which only look similar, and arduous, which has a different root; the near-meaning group lists words for strong feeling.
note.cn: 形近组提醒别与只是形似的 order、odor 以及词根不同的 arduous 混淆；近义组列出表示强烈感情的词。

entries.definition: Burning with enthusiasm.
Arrangement, or a command.
A smell, especially a bad one.
Demanding great effort.
Very strong feeling.
Eager devotion to a cause.
Intense warmth of feeling.
Lively interest and eagerness.

normalIntro.en: Ardor is ard-, burn, plus -or, a state: the state of burning inside, which is what enthusiasm feels like.
normalIntro.cn: ardor 就是 ard-「烧」加 -or「状态」：心里烧着的状态，正是热情的感觉。

normal.en: American ardor, British ardour; pick one and stay consistent.
normal.cn: 美式 ardor，英式 ardour；选一种并保持一致。

normal.en: It is uncountable: say great ardor, not an ardor.
normal.cn: 它不可数：说 great ardor，不说 an ardor。

normal.en: The adjective is ardent, the adverb ardently.
normal.cn: 形容词是 ardent，副词是 ardently。

normal.en: Use ardor for plus the cause or person.
normal.cn: 用 ardor for 加事业或人。

normal.en: Arid shares the burning root but means dry.
normal.cn: arid 共享「烧」词根，但意为干旱。

abstract.en: Picture a coal that stays red overnight.
abstract.cn: 想象一块整夜通红的炭。

abstract.en: Imagine a speech that warms a cold hall.
abstract.cn: 想象一场把冷厅讲热的演说。

abstract.en: Think of a fire that dies when nobody feeds it.
abstract.cn: 想象一堆没人添柴就熄的火。

examples.en: His ardor for reform never cooled.
examples.cn: 他对改革的热情从未冷却。

examples.en: The volunteers worked with real ardor.
examples.cn: 志愿者们带着真正的热情工作。

examples.en: Early ardor gave way to steady routine.
examples.cn: 起初的热情让位于平稳的日常。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：ard-「烧」+ -or「状态」——心里一直烧着的状态，就是热情 ardor。

root: 原始印欧词根 as-「烧」生出拉丁 ardere「燃烧」，名词 ardor「火焰、热切」经古法语 ardour 进入英语；美式去掉 u 拼作 ardor，同族还有 ardent 与 arid。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are one fire: heat you can measure, and the same heat used as a name for eager feeling.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项是同一团火：能测量的热，以及被借来称呼热切感情的同一种热。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the fire in the chest that keeps on burning
core.cn: 核心意象：胸口那团一直烧着的火

branches.en: A speech that warms a cold hall.
branches.cn: 把冷厅讲热的演说。

branches.en: Volunteers who never slow down.
branches.cn: 从不松劲的志愿者。

branches.en: The noon sun beating on stone.
branches.cn: 正午晒在石头上的太阳。

branches.en: A coal still red at dawn.
branches.cn: 天亮时仍通红的炭。

branches.en: Both are heat, literal or felt.
branches.cn: 两者都是热，实际的或感到的。

intro.en: Ardor is the burn root ard- plus -or; the same root builds ardent, ardently and, through drying, arid and aridity.
intro.cn: ardor 是「烧」词根 ard- 加 -or；同一词根构成 ardent、ardently，并经「干」义构成 arid 与 aridity。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is ardere, to burn, ardor, flame, and aridus, dry, which gives arid and aridity.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语层次是 ardere「燃烧」、ardor「火焰」与 aridus「干的」，后者产生 arid 与 aridity。

latinEntries.meaning: to burn, to be on fire

definition_zh: n. 军械库，武器库（美式拼作 armory）；（引申）可动用的手段总和
definition_en: A place where weapons are stored or made; by extension, the whole range of resources or arguments someone can draw on. American English spells it armory.
core_image: 一屋子挂满兵器，随时可以取用
scene: 城堡的军械库里挂满了长矛。 The castle armoury was lined with spears.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：armoury 指存放或制造武器的库房，美式拼写为 armory。

pos.zh: 军械库；武器库；手段总和

senses.title: A store of weapons
senses.definition: a room or building where arms are kept, and sometimes where they are manufactured
senses.definitionCN: 存放武器的房间或建筑，有时也指制造武器的场所
senses.example: The rebels seized the armoury before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 叛军在黎明前夺下了军械库。
senses.why: The Latin base is a chest or cupboard, so armoury is literally the cupboard for arms, a place defined by what it holds.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语底层是「柜子」，所以 armoury 字面就是「放武器的柜子」，一个由所存之物定义的场所。

senses.title: The range you can draw on
senses.definition: figuratively, the full set of skills, arguments or measures available to a person
senses.definitionCN: 比喻义，指一个人可动用的全部技能、论据或措施
senses.example: Patience is the strongest weapon in her armoury.
senses.exampleCN: 耐心是她手段中最有力的一件。
senses.why: The store image transfers neatly: skills sit ready on the wall like weapons, waiting to be taken down.
senses.whyCN: 库房的画面顺畅地转移过来：技能像武器一样挂在墙上待取。

intro.en: Armoury comes from Latin armarium, a chest or closet, from arma, weapons. Old French armoire kept the cupboard sense, while English specialised it to arms.
intro.cn: armoury 来自拉丁语 armarium「柜子、壁橱」，词根为 arma「武器」。古法语 armoire 保留「柜子」义，英语则把它专指武器存放处。

items.en: Arma meant weapons and gear, the base shared by arm, army, armour and armada.
items.cn: arma 意为武器与装备，是 arm、army、armour 与 armada 共有的词根。

items.en: Armarium named a chest or closet, originally for arms but later for books and valuables.
items.cn: armarium 指柜子或壁橱，最初放武器，后来也放书与贵重物品。

items.en: Old French armoire kept the furniture sense, which is why French armoire still means a wardrobe.
items.cn: 古法语 armoire 保留家具义，因此法语 armoire 至今仍指大衣柜。

items.en: English took the word for a place where arms are stored, narrowing the cupboard to weapons.
items.cn: 英语用这个词指存放武器的地方，把「柜子」收窄为武器。

items.en: Nineteenth-century writers began calling a person's stock of arguments their armoury.
items.cn: 19 世纪作者开始把一个人掌握的论据称为他的 armoury。

items.en: American reform dropped the u to give armory, while British usage kept armoury.

note.en: The look-alike group includes armoire, the French wardrobe from the same Latin chest; the near-meaning group lists other words for a store of supplies.
note.cn: 形近组包含 armoire——出自同一拉丁「柜子」的法式衣柜；近义组列出其他表示储备场所的词。

entries.definition: Covering worn against weapons.
A large French wardrobe.
The weapons themselves.
A large fleet of warships.
A store of weapons and matériel.
A place where stores are kept.

An accumulated reserve of supplies.

normalIntro.en: Armoury is armour plus the place ending -y: the room where the armour and arms hang ready.
normalIntro.cn: armoury 就是 armour 加场所后缀 -y：铠甲与兵器挂着待取的那间屋子。

normal.en: British armoury, American armory; both are correct.
normal.cn: 英式 armoury，美式 armory，都对。

normal.en: Armoury is the place; armament is the weapons.
normal.cn: armoury 是场所，armament 是武器。

normal.en: An armoury of arguments is the common figurative use.

normal.en: French armoire is the same root, but a wardrobe.

normal.en: The keeper is an armourer, with -er for a person.
normal.cn: 管理员叫 armourer，-er 表人。

examples.cn: 停火后两处军械库都被封存。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：armour「武器铠甲」+ -y「场所」——放武器的地方，就是军械库 armoury。

root: 拉丁语 arma「武器」生出 armarium「柜子」，古法语 armoire 保留家具义，英语收窄为存放武器之处作 armoury；19 世纪引申指可动用的手段总和，美式拼 armory。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are one store: a room where weapons hang ready, and the same room used as a picture for a person's ready skills.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项是同一个库房：武器挂着待取的房间，以及被借来比喻一个人待用技能的同一个房间。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a room hung with weapons, any of them ready to take down
core.cn: 核心意象：一屋子挂满兵器，随时可以取用

branches.en: Spears racked along a stone wall.

branches.en: Both are stocks kept ready for use.
branches.cn: 两者都是备好待用的存量。

intro.en: Armoury is armour plus the place suffix -y; the same root builds armourer, armament and disarm.
intro.cn: armoury 是 armour 加场所后缀 -y；同一词根还构成 armourer、armament 与 disarm。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is arma, weapons, and armarium, a chest, which also gives French armoire and English ambry.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语层次是 arma「武器」与 armarium「柜子」，后者还给出法语 armoire 与英语 ambry。

definition_zh: adj. 可归因于……的；可归属于某人或某单位的
definition_en: Able to be regarded as caused by, or as belonging to, a stated person or factor.
core_image: 一条箭头把结果指回它的来处
scene: 报告说这轮减产大半可归因于早霜。 The report said the shortfall was largely attributable to the early frost.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：attributable 指某结果能够被认定由某个原因造成，常与 to 连用。

pos.zh: 可归因于……的；可归属的

forms.label: 形容词原级（无屈折变化）

senses.title: Traceable to a cause
senses.definition: of a result or effect that can reasonably be said to be caused by a stated factor
senses.definitionCN: 指结果或影响可以合理地被认定由某个因素造成
senses.example: Half the delay was attributable to bad weather.
senses.exampleCN: 一半的延误可归因于恶劣天气。
senses.why: Attribute means to assign to, so adding -able gives the sense of a result that can be assigned back to a cause.
senses.whyCN: attribute 意为「归于」，加上 -able 便指某个结果能够被归回一个原因。

senses.title: Assignable to an owner
senses.definition: of income, costs or work that can be credited or charged to a particular person or unit
senses.definitionCN: 指收入、成本或工作可以记入某个人员或单位名下
senses.example: Only costs attributable to the project were repaid.
senses.exampleCN: 只有可归属该项目的成本获得报销。
senses.why: Accounting kept the assigning sense but dropped the causal one, so the arrow points to an owner instead of a cause.
senses.whyCN: 会计沿用「归属」义而舍去因果义，于是箭头指向所有者而非原因。

intro.en: Attributable is attribute plus -able; attribute comes from Latin attribuere, to assign to, from ad-, to, and tribuere, to allot, from tribus, tribe.
intro.cn: attributable 是 attribute 加 -able；attribute 来自拉丁语 attribuere「归于」，由 ad-「向」与 tribuere「分派」构成，而 tribuere 出自 tribus「部族」。

items.en: Latin tribus meant a tribe, one of the divisions among which goods and duties were shared out.
items.cn: 拉丁语 tribus 意为「部族」，即分配财物与义务时所依据的划分之一。

items.en: From it came tribuere, to assign or grant, originally to allot among the tribes.
items.cn: 由此产生 tribuere「分配、授予」，本义是按部族分派。

items.en: With ad-, to, added, attribuere meant to assign to, to attach a thing to its source.
items.cn: 加上 ad-「向」构成 attribuere「归于」，即把事物挂到它的来源上。

items.en: The participle attributus, assigned, is the form English took as its base.
items.cn: 分词 attributus「已被归于的」是英语取用的基础形式。

items.en: English adopted attribute in the fifteenth century as a verb and, later, as a noun.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪采用 attribute 作动词，后来又作名词。

items.en: The adjective with -able appears in the seventeenth century, chiefly in reasoning about causes.
items.cn: 带 -able 的形容词出现在十七世纪，主要用于因果推断。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the tribute family; the near-meaning group lists other words for something that can be traced back to a source.
note.cn: 形近组保留 tribute 词族；近义组列出其他表示可追溯到某来源的词。

The act of assigning a cause.
