normalIntro.en: Attributable is attribute plus -able: if a result can be attributed to something, it is attributable to it.
normalIntro.cn: attributable 是 attribute 加 -able：结果能被归到某原因，它就是可归因于该原因的。

normal.en: The fixed pattern is attributable to plus a cause.
normal.cn: 固定句式是 attributable to 加原因。

normal.en: Directly and largely are the commonest adverbs.
normal.cn: directly 与 largely 是最常见的搭配副词。

normal.en: Attributable risk is a set epidemiology term.
normal.cn: attributable risk 是流行病学术语。

normal.en: The noun is attribution, not attributableness.
normal.cn: 名词是 attribution，不用 attributableness。

normal.en: The negative form is unattributable.
normal.cn: 否定形式是 unattributable。

abstract.en: Picture an arrow drawn from effect back to cause.
abstract.cn: 想象一支从结果指回原因的箭头。

abstract.en: Imagine a ledger line charged to one project.
abstract.cn: 想象账簿上一笔记入某项目的支出。

abstract.en: Think of a label tied to a single source.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚系在唯一来源上的标签。

examples.en: The gain is attributable to lower costs.
examples.cn: 这项收益可归因于成本下降。

examples.en: Deaths attributable to heat rose sharply.
examples.cn: 可归因于高温的死亡人数急升。

examples.en: Revenue attributable to the region was small.
examples.cn: 可归属该地区的收入很少。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：at-「向」+ tribute「分派」+ -able「可……的」——能把结果分派回某原因的，就是 attributable。

root: 拉丁语 tribus「部族」生出 tribuere「按部族分派」，加 ad-「向」成 attribuere「归于」；英语 attribute 再加 -able，表示结果可被归回某原因或某主体。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses draw the same arrow backwards: from an effect to its cause, and from money or work to its owner.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项画的是同一支向后的箭头：从结果指向原因，从款项或工作指向其归属者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an arrow pointing a result back to where it came from
core.cn: 核心意象：一条箭头把结果指回它的来处

branches.en: A shortfall traced to early frost.
branches.cn: 追溯到早霜的减产。

branches.en: Delay blamed on bad weather.
branches.cn: 归于恶劣天气的延误。

branches.en: Costs charged to one project.
branches.cn: 记入某项目的成本。

branches.en: Revenue credited to a region.
branches.cn: 归入某地区的收入。

branches.en: Both send the result back to a source.
branches.cn: 两者都把结果送回某个来源。

intro.en: Attributable is at- plus tribute plus -able; the tribute root also builds contribute, distribute and retribution.
intro.cn: attributable 是 at- 加 tribute 加 -able；tribute 词根还构成 contribute、distribute 与 retribution。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is tribus, tribe, tribuere, to allot, and attribuere, to assign to; -able is the Latin -abilis.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语层次是 tribus「部族」、tribuere「分派」与 attribuere「归于」；-able 即拉丁语 -abilis。

definition_zh: 栖息地；生境；（动植物的）自然生长地；居住环境
definition_en: the natural area in which a plant, animal, or other organism normally lives and finds the conditions it needs
core_image: 一片恰好为某种生命备好条件的地方，它自己走进去住下
scene: 这里指「栖息地」。 Biologists found that the restored marsh had become a habitat for three rare bird species.
sceneCN: 这里 habitat 是「天然栖息地」（第 1 个义项：动植物自然生活并获取所需条件的区域）；句意：生物学家发现，修复后的沼泽已成为三种珍稀鸟类的栖息地。场景要点：一片浅水与芦苇、几种在水面筑巢的鸟、鸟与这片地方之间“住进去”的关系。

pos.zh: 栖息地；生境；自然生长地
（人类或人造的）居住环境；居所（较新用法）

derivatives.zh: 无人居住的；荒无人烟的

senses.title: The natural home of a species
senses.definition: the natural environment in which a particular plant or animal lives and finds food, shelter and the conditions it needs
senses.definitionCN: 某种植物或动物自然生活、并获得食物、庇护和所需条件的环境
senses.example: Drainage destroyed the habitat of several native frogs.
senses.exampleCN: 排水工程毁掉了数种本地蛙类的栖息地。
senses.why: The Latin word is literally 'it inhabits'. A habitat is not a house that someone builds but a place an organism already occupies because the conditions suit it; the core image is a creature entering a place prepared by nature.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁词字面就是“它居住”。栖息地不是谁建造的房子，而是生物因条件合适而本来就占据的地方；核心意象是一只生物走进一片由自然备好的地方。

senses.title: The recorded locality of a species
senses.definition: the specific locality recorded for a plant or animal in its scientific description, or the area over which it occurs
senses.definitionCN: 科学描述中为某种动植物记录的特定地点，或该物种出现的区域
senses.example: The type specimen's habitat is a single valley in Yunnan.
senses.exampleCN: 那份模式标本的产地是云南的一条山谷。
senses.why: In 1762 the word began as a technical label in Latin descriptions of plants and animals: the part of the entry that told readers where the species lives. It names a point on the map, not a way of life.
senses.whyCN: 1762 年，这个词最初是拉丁文动植物描述中的一个技术标签：条目里告诉读者该物种住在哪里的一部分。它命名的是地图上的一点，而不是一种生活方式。

senses.title: A type of living space: wetland, forest, reef
senses.titleCN: 生境类型：湿地、森林、礁区
senses.definition: a category of environment defined by its physical conditions and the community of organisms it supports
senses.definitionCN: 由其物理条件及所供养的生物群落所定义的一类环境
senses.example: Coral reefs are the most diverse marine habitat.
senses.exampleCN: 珊瑚礁是多样性最高的海洋生境。
senses.why: Once many species' places are compared, the word groups them by type. The same 'place where life fits' becomes a category, so one can speak of a wetland habitat or a forest habitat.
senses.whyCN: 当许多物种的地方被放在一起比较，这个词就按类型把它们归类。同一个“生命得以安放之处”变成了类别，于是可以说湿地生境或森林生境。

senses.title: A designed home in captivity
senses.titleCN: 圈养环境：人工布置的栖息处
senses.definition: an enclosure or setting designed to imitate an animal's natural conditions in a zoo, aquarium, or laboratory
senses.definitionCN: 在动物园、水族馆或实验室中模仿动物自然条件而设计的围栏或环境
senses.example: The keepers rebuilt the enclosure to give the otters a more natural habitat.
senses.exampleCN: 饲养员重建了围栏，给水獭一个更自然的栖息环境。
senses.why: Here humans draw the boundary and supply the conditions. The word still means 'where the animal lives', but the place is now made rather than found.
senses.whyCN: 这里由人划定边界、提供条件。词义仍是“动物生活的地方”，但这片地方是被造出来的，而不是被找到的。

senses.title: Human or constructed living environment
senses.titleCN: 人类或人造的居住环境
senses.definition: a place designed for humans or other organisms to live in, including space stations and imagined colonies
senses.definitionCN: 为人类或其他生物居住而设计的地方，包括空间站与设想的定居点
senses.example: Engineers tested how a sealed lunar habitat would recycle water.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师测试了一座密封的月球居住舱将如何循环用水。
senses.why: The word extends from animals to humans when the emphasis is on the conditions that make life possible. A space habitat is an environment engineered to keep a living community alive.
senses.whyCN: 当重点落在“使生命得以维持的条件”上，这个词便从动物扩展到人类。太空居住舱就是一个为维持生命群落而工程化设计的环境。

senses.title: A micro-habitat for microbes
senses.definition: the specific small-scale conditions in which a microorganism or a cell population lives, such as a gut or a hot spring
senses.definitionCN: 微生物或细胞群体生活的特定小尺度条件，如肠道或温泉
senses.example: The acidic pool is a habitat for bacteria found nowhere else.
senses.exampleCN: 这个酸性水潭是别处找不到的细菌的栖息地。
senses.why: Scale is irrelevant to the core image: a few millilitres of hot spring can be as much a home as a forest, as long as the conditions fit the organism.
senses.whyCN: 尺度与核心意象无关：几毫升的温泉水和一片森林一样可以成为家，只要条件适合该生物。

senses.title: Figurative: a place where something thrives
senses.titleCN: 比喻：某事物得以繁衍的土壤
senses.definition: a setting or environment in which a particular activity, idea, or group can grow and persist
senses.definitionCN: 某种活动、观念或群体得以生长并持续的环境
senses.example: The old harbour became a habitat for small theatres and cheap studios.
senses.exampleCN: 旧港区成了小剧场和廉价工作室的滋生地。
senses.why: The biological meaning is transferred to ideas and institutions: if a place supplies the conditions that let a thing live, then it is that thing's habitat, even without soil or water.
senses.whyCN: 生物义被转移到观念与机构：如果一个地方提供了让某事物存活的条件，那它就是该事物的栖息地，哪怕没有土壤和水。

senses.title: Older general sense: a dwelling place
senses.definition: in 19th-century general use, simply a place where a person or thing dwells; now mostly literary or technical
senses.definitionCN: 在 19 世纪的一般用法中，泛指人或物居住的地方；现在多用于文学或技术语境
senses.example: The cottage had been his habitat for forty years.
senses.exampleCN: 那间小屋曾是他四十年的居所。
senses.why: The general sense 'dwelling place' is recorded from 1854, before ecology fixed the word to non-human life. Modern usage usually keeps habitat for organisms and leaves human homes to habitation or home.
senses.whyCN: “居住地”这一泛义从 1854 年就有记录，早于生态学把这个词固定用于非人类生命。现代用法通常把 habitat 留给生物，把人的住所交给 habitation 或「住所」一类的词。

intro.en: Habitat is a Latin verb form that English borrowed as a scientific noun: literally 'it inhabits'. Dates and the ecological extension are approximate.
intro.cn: habitat 是一个被英语当作科学名词借入的拉丁语动词形式，字面意为“它居住”。年代与生态学扩展的时间为大致估计。

items.en: First recorded as a technical term in Latin texts on English flora and fauna. It was the Modern Latin word beginning the part of a species description that told its locality.
items.cn: 最早记录于 1762 年，是英国动植物拉丁文志书中的技术术语。它是现代拉丁语词，用在物种描述中说明产地的那一部分开头。

items.en: Habitat is literally 'it inhabits', the third person singular present indicative of Latin habitare 'to live, dwell, inhabit'.
items.cn: habitat 字面就是“它居住”，是拉丁语 habitare“生活、居住、栖居”的第三人称单数现在时直陈式。

items.en: Habitare is a frequentative of habere 'to have, hold, possess', so dwelling was pictured as holding a place. English also took habit, inhabit and habitation from the same stem.
items.cn: habitare 是 habere“拥有、握有、占有”的反复动词，因此“居住”被想象成“握有一个地方”。英语也从同一词干借入 habit、inhabit 与 habitation。

items.en: Habere is reconstructed to PIE *ghabh- 'to give or receive', whose basic sense was probably 'to hold'. The root is reconstructed, not attested in writing.
items.cn: habere 被重构为原始印欧语 *ghabh-“给予或接受”，其基本义很可能是“握有”。该词根是重构的，没有书面文献直接记录。

items.en: The general sense 'dwelling place' is first attested in 1854, showing the word escaping from purely botanical and zoological writing.
items.cn: “居住地”这一泛义最早见于 1854 年，说明这个词开始越出纯粹的植物学与动物学写作。

items.en: Ecology turns habitat into a central countable noun: habitat loss, habitat fragmentation, habitat restoration. The compounds belong to modern conservation language rather than to the Latin source.
items.cn: 生态学把 habitat 变成核心的可数名词：habitat loss、habitat fragmentation、habitat restoration。这些复合词属于现代保护生物学语言，而不是拉丁语源。

note.en: The first group separates habitat from the words built on the same habere stem, since they look close but describe different things; the second group compares the scales and units of the living environment.
note.cn: 第一组把 habitat 与同一 habere 词干上的词分开，因为它们形近却描述不同事物；第二组比较“生存环境”的不同尺度与单位。

entries.definition: the act of living in a place, or a place to live in, especially a human dwelling. Habitat is where a species lives; habitation is the human act or building of living there.
entries.definitionCN: 居住的行为，或居住的地方，尤指人的住所。habitat 是物种生活之处；habitation 是人居住的行为或建筑。

entries.definition: to live or dwell in a place. It is the verb that habitat presupposes: a habitat is the place that a species inhabits.
entries.definitionCN: 居住于某地。它是 habitat 所预设的动词：栖息地就是某物种栖居的地方。

entries.definition: one who lives in a place, as opposed to a visitor. It names the occupant, while habitat names the occupied place.
entries.definitionCN: 居住在某地者，区别于访客。它命名占据者，而 habitat 命名被占据的地方。

entries.definition: a settled practice or tendency; also an old word for dress. It shares the 'hold' root but has nothing to do with where a species lives.
entries.definitionCN: 固定的习惯或倾向；也可旧指衣着。它共享“握有”词根，但与物种住在哪里无关。

entries.definition: the whole set of surrounding conditions, physical and social, that affect an organism. Environment is broader than habitat: it includes climate, neighbours and human pressure, not only the place occupied.
entries.definitionCN: 影响某一生物的全部周围条件，包括物理的与社会的。environment 比 habitat 更广：它包含气候、邻近生物与人类压力，而不只是被占据的地点。

entries.definition: a community of organisms together with the physical surroundings they interact with. An ecosystem is a working system; a habitat is one species' address inside it.
entries.definitionCN: 生物群落与其相互作用的物理环境之整体。ecosystem 是一个运转的系统；habitat 则是其中某一物种的“地址”。

entries.definition: the role and position a species occupies in an ecosystem, including what it eats and when it is active. Niche is the job; habitat is the workplace.
entries.definitionCN: 某物种在生态系统中的角色与位置，包括吃什么、何时活动。niche 是“职业”，habitat 是“工作场所”。

entries.definition: the entire geographical area over which a species occurs. A range may contain many habitats; a habitat is one patch of suitable conditions inside it.
entries.definitionCN: 某物种出现的整个地理区域。range 可以包含许多栖息地；habitat 则是其中一个条件合适的斑块。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: Latin habitare 'to dwell', habere 'to hold', and the English family inhabit / inhabitant / habitation.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与真实同族词：拉丁语 habitare“居住”、habere“握有”，以及英语词族 inhabit／inhabitant／habitation。

normal.en: Habitat is a whole Latin sentence compressed into a noun: habitat = 'it lives here'. The animal is the subject, the place is the object.
normal.cn: habitat 是一个压成名词的完整拉丁句子：habitat＝“它住在这里”。动物是主语，地方是宾语。

normal.en: Inhabit is the verb, inhabitant is the person or animal, habitation is the act or building, and habitat is the place itself: four roles from one stem.
normal.cn: inhabit 是动词，inhabitant 是居住者，habitation 是居住行为或住所，habitat 是地方本身：同一词干的四种角色。

normal.en: A habit is something you hold onto and repeat; a habitat is a place a species holds. The shared idea is 'holding', not 'living'.
normal.cn: habit 是你反复握持的习惯；habitat 是一个物种握有的地方。共同的想法是“握有”，而不是“居住”。

normal.en: Habitat loss is the standard conservation phrase: the place disappears, and the species has nowhere to be its subject.
normal.cn: habitat loss 是保护生物学的标准说法：地方消失了，物种也就无处可做那个主语。

normal.en: In a zoo, the enclosure is called a habitat only when it imitates the natural conditions closely enough.
normal.cn: 在动物园里，只有足够逼真地模仿自然条件的围栏才被称为 habitat。

abstract.en: Picture a marsh at dawn: reeds, shallow water, three birds already there. Nobody invited them; the place simply fits, and that fit is habitat.
abstract.cn: 想象清晨的沼泽：芦苇、浅水、三只已经在那里的鸟。没人邀请它们，地方只是恰好合适，而这种“合适”就是 habitat。

abstract.en: Scale does not matter: a forest, a reef, a puddle, or a length of intestine can all be a habitat if the conditions let a life continue there.
abstract.cn: 尺度无关紧要：森林、礁区、水洼或一段肠道，只要条件能让生命在那里延续，都可以是栖息地。

abstract.en: Move the word from biology to culture and the same logic holds: whatever supplies the conditions for a thing to live is that thing's habitat.
abstract.cn: 把这个词从生物学移到文化上，逻辑仍然成立：凡是提供某事物存活条件的地方，就是该事物的栖息地。

examples.en: The dam cut the river's flow and dried out the habitat downstream.
examples.cn: 大坝截断了河流的水量，使下游的栖息地干涸。

examples.en: Polar bears are hard to study in their habitat because the ice is moving.
examples.cn: 北极熊在自然栖息地中很难研究，因为冰面一直在移动。

examples.en: The abandoned rail yard became a habitat for foxes, moths and rare grasses.
examples.cn: 废弃的铁路场成了狐狸、飞蛾与稀有草类的栖息地。

dict_mnemonic.text: “哈比塔特”——哈比（鸟）塔（搭）特（别）舒服的窝，住进去就不走了 → habitat 栖息地

root: 拉丁语 habitat 字面意为“它居住”，源自 habitare“居住”、habere“握有”，核心是“生命自己走进并占住的一片合适之地”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of habitat, all grown from one relation: a living thing and a place whose conditions fit it, so that the place becomes where it lives.
sensesIntro.cn: habitat 的八个义项都从同一种关系长出来：一个生命与一片条件合适的地方，于是这片地方成为它生活之处。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a creature enters a place whose conditions already suit it and settles there.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只生物走进一片条件本就适合它的地方，并在那里安顿下来。

branches.en: NATURAL HOME: one species' place and a whole class of places such as wetland or reef both answer the same question — where does life fit?
branches.cn: 天然家园：单一物种的地方与湿地、礁区等整类地方，回答的都是同一个问题——生命在哪里合适？

branches.en: LOCALITY: in a scientific description the word narrows to a point on the map, the recorded place where the species was found.
branches.cn: 产地：在科学描述中，这个词收窄为地图上的一点，即记录到该物种的地点。

branches.en: MADE AND MICRO: a zoo enclosure or a hot spring is still a habitat if the conditions, however constructed or small, let the organism live.
branches.cn: 人造与微观：动物园围栏或温泉仍是栖息地，只要条件——无论多么人工或微小——能让该生物存活。

branches.en: HUMAN: the word moves to engineered living environments such as space stations, where the point is keeping a community alive.
branches.cn: 人类：这个词移到空间站等工程化居住环境，重点在于维持一个生命群落的存续。

branches.en: EXTENSION: ideas can have a habitat too, and the old general sense simply called any dwelling place a habitat.
branches.cn: 扩展：观念也可以有栖息地；旧有的泛义则把任何居住地都称作 habitat。

intro.en: Habitat is not built from an English prefix at all: it is a Latin verb ending borrowed as a noun. Its apparent parts belong to Latin, and English later adds -ant, -ation, -able and in- to the same stem.
intro.cn: habitat 根本不是由英语前缀构成的：它是把拉丁语动词词尾当作名词借入。它表面上的成分属于拉丁语，英语后来又在同一词干上加 -ant、-ation、-able 与 in-。

latinIntro.en: The family rests on habere 'to have, hold, possess' and its frequentative habitare 'to dwell'. Habitare gives habitat, habitation and inhabit; habere also gives habit, able and exhibit through older French and Latin paths.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词族建立在 habere“拥有、握有、占有”及其反复动词 habitare“居住”上。habitare 给出 habitat、habitation、inhabit；habere 还经由较早的法语和拉丁语路径给出 habit、able、exhibit。

items.meaningCN: 居住于；栖居于（in- 在内 + habitare 居住）
items.example: Few fish can inhabit water this warm.
items.exampleCN: 很少有鱼能栖居在这么温暖的水里。

items.meaning: one who lives in a place
items.meaningCN: 居民；栖居者（-ant 表示施事者）
items.example: The island's only inhabitants are seabirds.
items.exampleCN: 岛上唯一的居民是海鸟。

items.meaning: the act of dwelling, or a dwelling place
items.meaningCN: 居住；住所（-ion 构成行为或地点名词）
items.example: The valley shows signs of human habitation for centuries.
items.exampleCN: 这条山谷显示出数百年人类居住的痕迹。

items.meaningCN: 可居住的；适宜居住的（-able 表示能够被）
items.example: The planet lies just inside the habitable zone.
items.exampleCN: 这颗行星恰好位于宜居带内侧。

items.meaningCN: 无人居住的；荒无人烟的
items.example: The island was uninhabited for most of the year.
items.exampleCN: 这座岛一年中大部分时间无人居住。

items.meaning: to live together, especially as a couple
items.meaningCN: 同居；共同居住（co- 共同 + 居住）
items.example: The two species cohabit in the same cave.
items.exampleCN: 这两个物种共同栖息在同一洞穴中。

items.structure: Latin habitus 'condition, demeanour, dress', from habere
items.meaning: a settled practice; also an old word for clothing
items.meaningCN: 习惯；旧指衣着（来自拉丁语 habitus“状态、举止、衣着”）
items.example: Reading before sleep had become a habit.
items.exampleCN: 睡前阅读已成了一种习惯。

items.meaningCN: 习惯性的；惯常的（-ual 构成形容词）
items.example: His habitual lateness annoyed the group.
items.exampleCN: 他惯常的迟到让全组不满。

items.meaning: to accustom someone or something to a condition
items.example: Animals habituate quickly to the sound of the generator.
items.exampleCN: 动物很快会习惯发电机的声音。

items.meaning: to hold out for others to see; to display
items.meaningCN: 展出；显示（ex- 向外 + habere 握有）
items.example: The museum exhibits specimens from the same habitat.
items.exampleCN: 博物馆展出来自同一栖息地的标本。

items.meaning: having the power or skill to do something
items.meaningCN: 能够的；有能力的（同一“握有”词根经法语演变）
items.example: The team was able to map the whole habitat.
items.exampleCN: 团队得以绘制整个栖息地的地图。

latinEntries.meaning: a dwelling; the act of dwelling

definition_zh: n. 两栖动物学（研究两栖动物的动物学分支）
definition_en: The branch of zoology that studies amphibians, their biology, life cycles, ecology and conservation.
core_image: 蹲在池塘边，一记就是半辈子蛙类笔记
scene: 她把二十年的蛙类观察记录整理成了一门课。 Amphibiology is a small but growing field.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：研究两栖动物的这门动物学分支就是 amphibiology。它规模不大，但随着两栖动物衰退问题受到关注而逐渐扩展。

pos.zh: 两栖动物学

senses.title: The discipline
senses.definition: the scientific study of amphibians, including their anatomy, breeding and life cycles
senses.definitionCN: 对两栖动物的科学研究，包括其解剖结构、繁殖与生活史
senses.example: She took her doctorate in amphibiology.
senses.exampleCN: 她取得了两栖动物学的博士学位。
senses.why: The word is amphi-, both, plus bios, life, plus -logy, study: the study of animals that live two lives, one in water and one on land.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是 amphi-「两者」加 bios「生命」加 -logy「学问」：研究那些过两种生活的动物，一种在水里，一种在陆上。

senses.title: The conservation branch
senses.definition: the applied side of the field, concerned with declining populations and habitat loss
senses.definitionCN: 该学科的应用方向，关注种群衰退与栖息地丧失
senses.example: Amphibiology now feeds directly into wetland policy.
senses.exampleCN: 两栖动物学如今直接为湿地政策提供依据。
senses.why: Because amphibian skin absorbs whatever is in the water, the discipline became an early warning system for whole ecosystems.
senses.whyCN: 由于两栖动物的皮肤会吸收水中的任何物质，这门学科成了整个生态系统的早期预警系统。

intro.en: Amphibiology is assembled from three Greek pieces: amphi-, both or on both sides, bios, life, and -logia, study. It names the study of animals with two lives.
intro.cn: amphibiology 由三个希腊语部件拼成：amphi-「两者、两边」，bios「生命」，以及 -logia「学问」。它命名的是对「过两种生活的动物」的研究。

items.en: Greek amphi meant on both sides or around. It gives amphibious, amphitheatre and amphora, all built on the idea of two sides.
items.cn: 希腊语 amphi 意为「在两边、环绕」。它产生 amphibious、amphitheatre 与 amphora，都建立在「两边」这个想法上。

items.en: Greek bios meant life or a way of living. It is the base of biology, biography and biosphere.
items.cn: 希腊语 bios 意为「生命、生活方式」。它是 biology、biography 与 biosphere 的底座。

items.en: Greek amphibios meant living a double life, of land and water. Aristotle already used it for animals that breathe both ways.
items.cn: 希腊语 amphibios 意为「过双重生活的」，指陆与水两种。亚里士多德已用它指两种方式呼吸的动物。

items.en: Modern scientific Latin joined amphibio- to -logia to name a speciality inside zoology, alongside herpetology and ichthyology.
items.cn: 现代科学拉丁语把 amphibio- 与 -logia 拼合，为动物学内部的一个专业方向命名，与 herpetology、ichthyology 并列。

items.en: English took amphibiology as the field grew in the twentieth century, and the practitioner is an amphibologist.
items.cn: 英语在 20 世纪该领域扩展时借入 amphibiology，从业者称 amphibologist。

note.en: The look-alike group warns against amphibology, which means ambiguity, not frogs; the near-meaning group lists neighbouring branches of zoology.
note.cn: 形近组提醒别与 amphibology 混淆，后者意为「歧义」而非蛙类；近义组列出动物学的相邻分支。

entries.definition: An animal that lives in water and on land.
Able to operate in water and on land.
entries.definitionCN: 能在水中和陆上活动的。

entries.definition: Ambiguity of expression, a double meaning.
The study of living things.
The study of reptiles and amphibians.
entries.definitionCN: 对爬行动物与两栖动物的研究。

entries.definition: The study of animals.
The study of fishes.
The study of organisms and their surroundings.
entries.definitionCN: 对生物及其环境的研究。

normalIntro.en: Amphibiology is amphi plus bio plus logy: both, life, study, so the study of two-life animals.
normalIntro.cn: amphibiology 就是 amphi 加 bio 加 logy：两者、生命、学问，即对「两种生活的动物」的研究。

normal.en: Amphi means both, bio means life, logy means study.
normal.cn: amphi 意为「两者」，bio 意为「生命」，logy 意为「学问」。

normal.en: Keep the i: amphibiology is frogs, amphibology is ambiguity.
normal.cn: 留住那个 i：amphibiology 讲蛙类，amphibology 讲歧义。

normal.en: It is uncountable: amphibiology, not an amphibiology.
normal.cn: 它不可数：amphibiology，不说 an amphibiology。

normal.en: The person is an amphibologist, with -logist.
normal.cn: 从业者是 amphibologist，用 -logist。

normal.en: Herpetology covers reptiles too, so it is the wider label.
normal.cn: herpetology 还涵盖爬行动物，所以是更宽的标签。

abstract.en: Picture a notebook full of frog sketches beside a pond.
abstract.cn: 想象池塘边一本画满蛙类速写的笔记。

abstract.en: Imagine a tadpole turning into a frog under a lens.
abstract.cn: 想象镜头下一只蝌蚪变成蛙。

abstract.en: Think of a quiet wetland that tells you how clean the water is.
abstract.cn: 想象一片安静的湿地，告诉你水有多干净。

examples.en: Amphibiology draws on ecology and genetics alike.
examples.cn: 两栖动物学同时借鉴生态学与遗传学。

examples.en: Her work in amphibiology changed local wetland rules.
examples.cn: 她在两栖动物学方面的工作改变了当地湿地规定。

examples.en: Few universities offer a full course in amphibiology.
examples.cn: 很少有大学开设完整的两栖动物学课程。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：amphi「两边」+ bio「生命」+ logy「学问」——研究在水陆两边过日子的生命，就是两栖动物学。

root: 希腊语 amphi「两边」+ bios「生命」构成 amphibios「过双重生活的」，再加 -logia「学问」，经科学拉丁语拼合为 amphibiology，字面即「研究两种生活的动物之学」。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are one speciality: the pure study of two-life animals, and the same knowledge put to work protecting them.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项是同一个专业方向：对「两种生活的动物」的纯粹研究，以及把同一套知识用于保护它们。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lifetime of frog notes kept beside a pond
core.cn: 核心意象：在池塘边记了半辈子的蛙类笔记

branches.en: A thesis on frog breeding calls.
branches.cn: 一篇关于蛙类求偶鸣叫的论文。

branches.en: A life cycle traced from egg to adult.
branches.cn: 从卵到成体的生活史追踪。

branches.en: A survey that closes a polluted pond.
branches.cn: 一次导致关闭污染池塘的调查。

branches.en: Skin used as a water-quality gauge.
branches.cn: 把皮肤当作水质标尺。

branches.en: One field, pure then applied.
branches.cn: 同一个领域，先纯粹研究，再应用。

intro.en: Amphibiology is a three-part Greek compound, and each part builds a whole shelf of English scientific words.
intro.cn: amphibiology 是三段式希腊语复合词，每个部件都能撑起一整架英语科学词汇。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin layer here: amphi, bios and logos are all Greek, joined in modern scientific Latin only as a naming convention.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁语层次：amphi、bios 与 logos 全是希腊语，只是在现代科学拉丁语的命名习惯中拼合起来。

definition_zh: 媒体；传媒；传播媒介；（medium 的复数）介质、媒介
definition_en: the organizations and channels that spread news and information to the public, or the plural of medium in the sense of a substance or channel
core_image: 许多人站在同一条传声管道两侧：信息从一头进去，从另一头被所有人听见
scene: 这里指「媒体」。 The story reached the public through three national media outlets within an hour.
sceneCN: 这里 media 是「媒体机构、传媒」（第 2 个义项：报纸、电视、网站等新闻机构）；句意：这条新闻在一小时内经由三家全国性媒体机构传到了公众耳中。场景要点：三块不同的屏幕、同一条正在播出的新闻、屏幕前抬头看的人。

pos.zh: 媒体；传媒（报纸、广播、网络等机构的总称）
medium 的复数：媒介；介质；手段

forms.label: 复数（单数为 medium；作“传媒”时通常与单数同形）

senses.title: The media as a collective body
senses.definition: newspapers, broadcasting, and online news organizations considered together as one social force
senses.definitionCN: 把报纸、广播和网络新闻机构合在一起，视为一股社会力量
senses.example: The media ignored the report for a week.
senses.exampleCN: 媒体有一个星期没有理会这份报告。
senses.why: Many separate channels are treated as one thing because they all stand between events and the public. The plural form becomes a collective name for that middle layer.
senses.whyCN: 许多彼此分开的渠道被当作一个东西，因为它们都站在事件与公众之间。复数形式于是变成了这一中间层的集合名称。

senses.title: News organizations and journalists
senses.definition: the specific outlets, editors, and reporters who gather and publish news
senses.definitionCN: 采集并发布新闻的具体机构、编辑与记者
senses.example: Three media outlets carried the story on their front pages.
senses.exampleCN: 三家媒体机构把这条新闻放上了头版。
senses.why: Here the collective is broken back into its members. Media is short for media organizations, and the word points to the people and desks doing the work.
senses.whyCN: 这里集合体又被拆回它的成员。media 是 media organizations 的简写，词指向的是做这份工作的人与编辑部。

senses.title: Channels of communication
senses.definition: the different means by which a message is carried to an audience, such as print, radio, or film
senses.definitionCN: 把信息送达受众的不同手段，如印刷、广播或电影
senses.example: Print and broadcast are different media for the same message.
senses.exampleCN: 印刷与广播是传递同一条信息的两种不同媒介。
senses.why: Medium means 'that which stands in the middle'. A channel stands between a message and its audience, so each channel is a medium and several are media.
senses.whyCN: medium 意为“处在中间的东西”。渠道站在信息与受众之间，所以每个渠道是一个 medium，多个渠道就是 media。

senses.title: Plural of medium: substances that carry something
senses.titleCN: medium 的复数：承载某物的介质
senses.definition: the plural of medium for a physical substance through which light, sound, or another effect travels
senses.definitionCN: medium 的复数，指光、声音或其他效应在其中传播的物理物质
senses.example: Sound travels through different media at different speeds.
senses.exampleCN: 声音在不同介质中的传播速度不同。
senses.why: Air, water and glass each sit between a source and a receiver. This is the oldest physical sense of medium, and media is simply its plural.
senses.whyCN: 空气、水、玻璃都位于源头与接收者之间。这是 medium 最古老的物理义，而 media 只是它的复数。

senses.title: Social media as platforms
senses.definition: the online platforms on which users create and share content with one another
senses.definitionCN: 用户在其中创作并相互分享内容的网络平台
senses.example: The campaign spread through social media in two days.
senses.exampleCN: 这场活动两天内就通过社交媒体传开了。
senses.why: The channel no longer belongs to a publisher: every user is also a sender. The old 'middle layer' becomes a set of platforms in the middle of everyone.
senses.whyCN: 渠道不再属于出版方：每个用户同时也是发送者。旧的“中间层”变成了位于所有人中间的一组平台。

senses.title: Storage media
senses.definition: the physical materials or devices on which data is kept, such as disks or tapes
senses.definitionCN: 用来保存数据的物理材料或设备，如磁盘或磁带
senses.example: The archive was moved to newer storage media.
senses.exampleCN: 档案被转移到了更新的存储介质上。
senses.why: Data has to sit in something. The storage material stands between the data and the machine that reads it, so it is a medium and several are media.
senses.whyCN: 数据必须待在某种东西里。存储材料站在数据与读取它的机器之间，所以它是一个 medium，多个就是 media。

senses.title: Art media: the materials of a work
senses.titleCN: 艺术媒介：作品所用的材料
senses.definition: the materials an artist uses, such as oil, watercolour, clay, or video
senses.definitionCN: 艺术家使用的材料，如油画颜料、水彩、黏土或影像
senses.example: The artist works in mixed media.
senses.exampleCN: 这位艺术家使用综合媒材创作。
senses.why: Paint and clay are substances that carry an image the way wire carries a signal. The plural media names the set of such materials.
senses.whyCN: 颜料与黏土是承载图像的物质，就像导线承载信号。复数 media 命名这样一组材料。

senses.title: Culture media in biology
senses.definition: the plural of medium for the nutrient substances in which microorganisms or cells are grown
senses.definitionCN: medium 的复数，指培养微生物或细胞所用的营养基质
senses.example: The bacteria were grown on three different culture media.
senses.exampleCN: 这些细菌在三种不同的培养基上培养。
senses.why: A culture medium is the substance between a cell and its nutrients. It is a technical survival of the Latin sense, kept alive in laboratories.
senses.whyCN: 培养基是细胞与其养分之间的物质。它是拉丁义项在实验室里保留下来的技术性用法。

intro.en: Media is the plural of medium, which English took from Latin in the 1580s. The 'news media' sense is a 20th-century development; the dates below are those given by standard etymological references.
intro.cn: media 是 medium 的复数，medium 于 16 世纪 80 年代由拉丁语进入英语。“新闻传媒”这一义项是 20 世纪的产物；以下年代采用通行词源资料的说法。

items.en: Media is first recorded in English meaning 'newspapers, radio, TV, etc.', perhaps abstracted from mass-media. The plural form was reinterpreted as a collective singular.
items.cn: media 于 1927 年首次在英语中记录为“报纸、广播、电视等”，可能是从 mass-media 中提取出来的。这个复数形式被重新解释为一个集合单数。

items.en: Mass-media, with the singular mass-medium, is recorded as a technical term in advertising. It named the means of communication that reach large numbers of people.
items.cn: mass-media（单数作 mass-medium）于 1923 年作为广告业的技术术语有记录。它指能到达大量人群的传播手段。

items.en: Medium entered English meaning 'a middle ground, quality, or degree; that which holds a middle place'. It came from Latin medium, the neuter of medius 'in the middle'.
items.cn: medium 于 16 世纪 80 年代进入英语，意为“中间地带、中间性质或程度；处于中间位置的东西”。它来自拉丁语 medium，即 medius“在中间”的中性形式。

items.en: Latin medium meant 'the middle, midst, center; interval'. The sense 'intervening substance through which a force is conveyed' is recorded in English from the 1590s, and 'channel of communication' from about 1600.
items.cn: 拉丁语 medium 意为“中间、中央、间隔”。英语中“力量借以传递的中间物质”这一义项从 16 世纪 90 年代有记录，“传播渠道”义约从 1600 年起有记录。

items.en: Medium goes back to PIE *medhyo- 'middle', the root also behind mediate, median, medieval (medium aevum) and Mediterranean.
items.cn: medium 可追溯到原始印欧语 *medhyo-“中间”，该词根也是 mediate、median、medieval（medium aevum）与 Mediterranean 的来源。

items.en: The print-publication sense of medium is from 1795 and fed the later media. In current usage media as 'the press and broadcasters' takes either a plural or a singular verb, while media as the plural of medium remains plural.
items.cn: medium 的“印刷出版物”义始于 1795 年，并滋养了后来的 media。在当代用法中，表示“新闻与广播机构”的 media 可接复数动词也可接单数动词；而作为 medium 复数的 media 仍是复数。

note.en: The first group separates the singular medium, the rare plural medias, the process noun mediation and the statistical median. The second group compares media with mass media, social media, the press and a plain channel.
note.cn: 第一组区分单数 medium、罕见复数 medias、过程名词 mediation 与统计学的 median；第二组把 media 与 mass media、social media、the press 以及普通的 channel 作比较。

entries.definition: one channel, substance, or means. It is the singular of media, and the pair keeps the Latin number distinction in careful writing.
entries.definitionCN: 一个渠道、一种物质或一种手段。它是 media 的单数；在严谨写作中，这对词保留拉丁语的单复数区别。

entries.definition: a rare double plural sometimes used for several communication channels. Because media is already the plural of medium, many editors reject it.
entries.definitionCN: 有时用来指多个传播渠道的罕见双重复数。由于 media 已是 medium 的复数，许多编辑不接受这种形式。

entries.definition: the act of helping two sides reach agreement. It comes from the verb mediate 'to stand in the middle', not from media as news organizations.
entries.definitionCN: 帮助双方达成一致的行为。它来自动词 mediate“站在中间”，而不是来自表示新闻机构的 media。

entries.definition: the middle value in a set of numbers, or a middle line. It shares the 'middle' root but belongs to measurement, not communication.
entries.definitionCN: 一组数字中的中间值，或一条中线。它共享“中间”词根，却属于测量，而不属于传播。

entries.definition: the media that reach very large audiences, such as television and national newspapers. It names the reach, while media alone can include small outlets.
entries.definitionCN: 能到达极大规模受众的媒体，如电视与全国性报纸。它命名的是覆盖范围，而单说 media 也可以包括小型机构。

entries.definition: platforms where users themselves create and share content. It is a subset of media in which the audience also publishes.
entries.definitionCN: 由用户自己创作并分享内容的平台。它是 media 的一个子集，在其中受众也同时发布内容。

entries.definition: newspapers and the journalists who work for them. It is narrower than media: the press is print-centred, while media includes broadcast and online.
entries.definitionCN: 报纸以及为其工作的记者。它比 media 窄：press 以印刷为中心，而 media 包括广播与网络。

entries.definition: a route through which something is passed. It is the plain word for the middle layer; media is the institutional and collective name for such channels.
entries.definitionCN: 某物借以传递的路径。它是描述中间层的平实词；media 则是这类渠道在机构与集合层面的名称。

normalIntro.en: Real grammar and real relatives: media is the plural of medium, from Latin medius 'middle', and the same root gives mediate, median and medieval.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实语法与真实同族词：media 是 medium 的复数，medium 来自拉丁语 medius“中间”，同一词根还给出 mediate、median、medieval。

normal.en: Media is the plural of medium. One channel is a medium; several channels are media, just as one datum becomes data.
normal.cn: media 是 medium 的复数。一个渠道是 medium，多个渠道就是 media，正如一个 datum 变成 data。

normal.en: Medium means 'the middle thing'. A newspaper stands in the middle between an event and its readers, so it is a medium of communication.
normal.cn: medium 意为“中间的那个东西”。报纸站在事件与读者之间，所以它是传播的媒介。

normal.en: Mass media and social media are compounds: one stresses reach, the other stresses that users publish too.
normal.cn: mass media 与 social media 都是复合词：前者强调覆盖范围，后者强调用户也在发布。

normal.en: Mediation is not media: mediate means 'to stand in the middle' between two sides, and mediation is the act of helping them agree.
normal.cn: mediation 不是 media：mediate 意为“站在两方中间”，mediation 是帮助他们达成一致的行为。

normal.en: In careful writing, 'the media are' and 'the media is' are both defended; the plural form is old, but the collective use is modern.
normal.cn: 在严谨写作中，“the media are”与“the media is”都有人辩护；复数形式是旧的，集合用法却是现代的。

abstract.en: Picture a pipe between two rooms. Whatever is shouted into one end comes out the other; the pipe itself is the medium.
abstract.cn: 想象两个房间之间的一根管道。从一端喊进去的东西从另一端出来；这根管道本身就是媒介。

abstract.en: When the pipe is owned by a few companies, it stops being just a pipe and becomes an institution with its own interests.
abstract.cn: 当这根管道被少数公司拥有，它就不再只是一根管道，而变成一个有自身利益的机构。

abstract.en: Social media removes the pipe: everyone holds an end of it, so the middle layer is made of the crowd itself.
abstract.cn: 社交媒体拆掉了管道：每个人都握着管道的一端，于是中间层由人群自己构成。

examples.en: The media were barred from the courtroom.
examples.cn: 媒体被禁止进入法庭。

examples.en: Water is a better medium for sound than air.
examples.cn: 水比空气更适合作为声音的介质。

examples.en: The gallery shows paintings, video and mixed media.
examples.cn: 这家画廊展出绘画、影像和综合媒材作品。

dict_mnemonic.text: “米迪亚”——米迪亚站在中间，把同一条消息递给了屋里的所有人 → media 媒体、媒介

root: media 是 medium“中间物、媒介”的复数，medium 来自拉丁语 medius“中间的”，核心是“站在信息与受众之间的那条渠道”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of media, all from one position: something placed in the middle, between a source and a receiver — a newspaper between an event and the public, air between a sound and an ear, or a disk between data and a machine.
sensesIntro.cn: media 的八个义项都来自同一个位置：某物被放在中间，位于源头与接收者之间——报纸在事件与公众之间，空气在声音与耳朵之间，磁盘在数据与机器之间。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a channel standing in the middle, carrying something from one side to the other.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条站在中间的渠道，把某物从一头送到另一头。

branches.en: THE COLLECTIVE: the middle layer can be named as one body, or broken back into the outlets and reporters that fill it.
branches.cn: 集合体：这一中间层可以被命名为一个整体，也可以拆回填满它的机构与记者。

branches.en: CHANNELS AND SUBSTANCES: a communication route and a physical medium are both what stands between source and receiver.
branches.cn: 渠道与物质：传播路径与物理介质，都是站在源头与接收者之间的东西。

branches.en: PLATFORMS: social media distributes the middle layer among the users themselves.
branches.cn: 平台：社交媒体把这一中间层分散到了用户自己手中。

branches.en: MATERIALS: a disk holds data and paint holds an image; in both cases the material is the medium.
branches.cn: 材料：磁盘承载数据，颜料承载图像；两种情形里，材料都是媒介。

branches.en: BIOLOGY: a culture medium is the nutrient layer between a cell and what feeds it.
branches.cn: 生物学：培养基是细胞与其养分之间那一层营养物质。

intro.en: Media is not built with an English suffix: it is the Latin plural of medium, and English later added -al, -an, -ate and -ation to the same root. Compounds such as multimedia and intermediary extend it further.
intro.cn: media 不是用英语后缀构成的：它是 medium 的拉丁语复数，英语后来在同一词根上加了 -al、-an、-ate、-ation。multimedia、intermediary 这类复合词进一步扩展了它。

latinIntro.en: Latin medius 'in the middle' gives the neuter noun medium 'the middle', the verb mediare 'to be in the middle, mediate', and the adjective medianus. English keeps the neuter plural media unchanged.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 medius“在中间”给出中性名词 medium“中间”，动词 mediare“处于中间、调解”，以及形容词 medianus。英语原样保留了中性复数 media。

items.meaning: channels or substances in the middle; the news media
items.meaningCN: 居于中间的渠道或介质；新闻传媒（拉丁中性复数 -a）
items.example: The media covered the trial every day.
items.exampleCN: 媒体每天都报道这场审判。

items.meaningCN: 一个渠道、一种介质或一种手段（拉丁语 medium“中间”）
items.example: Radio was the dominant medium of the 1930s.
items.exampleCN: 无线电广播是 20 世纪 30 年代的主导媒介。

items.meaningCN: 中间的；内侧的（-al 构成形容词）
items.example: The injury affected the medial ligament of the knee.
items.exampleCN: 伤及了膝盖内侧的韧带。

items.meaning: the middle value; situated in the middle
items.meaningCN: 中位数；中间的（-an 构成形容词与名词）
items.example: The median income rose slightly last year.
items.exampleCN: 去年的收入中位数略有上升。

items.meaning: to stand between two sides and help them agree
items.meaningCN: 调解；居中传达（-ate 构成动词）
items.example: A neutral official mediated the dispute.
items.exampleCN: 一位中立官员调解了这场争端。

items.meaningCN: 调解；调停（-ion 构成行为名词）
items.example: The talks ended in mediation rather than a strike.
items.exampleCN: 谈判以调解而非罢工收场。

items.meaningCN: 调解人；中间人（-or 表示行为者）
items.example: The mediator met both sides separately.
items.exampleCN: 调解人分别会见了双方。

items.meaning: content that combines several media forms
items.meaningCN: 多媒体；综合多种媒介的内容（multi- 多 + media）
items.example: The museum uses multimedia to explain the site.
items.exampleCN: 博物馆用多媒体来讲解这处遗址。

items.meaning: a person or body that acts between two sides
items.meaningCN: 中间人；中介机构（inter- 之间 + medi- 中间 + -ary）
items.example: The bank acted as an intermediary in the sale.
items.exampleCN: 银行在这笔交易中充当了中介。

items.meaningCN: 中世纪的（medi- 中间 + aevum 时代 + -al）
items.example: The town has a well-preserved medieval wall.
items.exampleCN: 这座镇子有一段保存完好的中世纪城墙。

items.meaning: the sea in the middle of the land
items.meaningCN: 地中海（medi- 中间 + terra 陆地 + -anean，字面“陆地中间的海”）
items.example: The ship crossed the Mediterranean in six days.
items.exampleCN: 这艘船用六天横渡了地中海。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 在中间的；位于两者之间的

latinEntries.meaning: to be in the middle; to mediate
